TER : la gratuité prolongée entre Diamniadio et l’AIBD jusqu’au 11 octobre
items.description: La gratuité du transport sur le tronçon Diamniadio-Aéroport international Blaise Diagne (AIBD) du Train express régional (TER) est prolongée jusqu’au 11 octobre 2026 inclus, ont annoncé la SENTER et la SETER. Initialement prévue jusqu’au 4 octobre, cette mesure est ainsi reconduite du 5 au 11 octobre, dans les deux sens de circulation. Elle intervient dans le cadre de la mise en service de la liaison ferroviaire desservant l’AIBD. Selon la SENTER et la SETER, cette prolongation vise notamment à permettre à davantage de voyageurs de découvrir la nouvelle desserte et de se familiariser avec les conditions de déplacement vers l’aéroport et les différentes localités desservies. La gratuité concerne exclusivement le tronçon Diamniadio-AIBD. Les trajets effectués sur le reste du réseau TER restent soumis aux tarifs en vigueur. Les deux structures invitent les usagers à consulter leurs canaux officiels pour obtenir des informations complémentaires sur la desserte.

items.title: La presse espagnole encense Yassir Zabiri, nouvelle "icône" du football marocain
items.description: Les performances remarquées de l’international marocain Yassir Zabiri avec le Racing Santander ont considérablement accru sa notoriété au Maroc, où l’attaquant est désormais devenu une « icône » du football marocain, écrit vendredi le quotidien espagnol El Diario Montañés. Auteur de six buts depuis le début de la saison en première division espagnole, le meilleur buteur du club cantabre figure désormais dans une campagne publicitaire déployée à travers le Royaume, aux côtés d’autres joueurs de la sélection nationale marocaine, précise le journal. Sur l’une des affiches de cette campagne, Zabiri apparaît vêtu de rouge, embrassant sa bague dans un geste de célébration après avoir marqué, avec pour slogan : « Une nouvelle année avec la détermination de réussir ». Déjà connu au Maroc, le jeune attaquant a vu sa popularité prendre une nouvelle dimension grâce à son début de saison prolifique en Liga, ainsi qu’à sa récente convocation en équipe nationale, souligne El Diario Montañés. Selon le quotidien, cet engouement profite également au Racing Santander, dont le nombre d’abonnés sur les réseaux sociaux a fortement progressé depuis l’annonce du recrutement de Zabiri, notamment auprès du public marocain. Pour rappel, LaLiga a désigné Yassir Zabiri meilleur joueur de moins de 23 ans du mois de septembre. L’attaquant marocain du Racing Santander a inscrit trois buts durant le mois et porte son total à six réalisations depuis le début de la saison 2026-2027. The post La presse espagnole encense Yassir Zabiri, nouvelle "icône" du football marocain appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ligue des nations : l’Italie et la France se neutralisent
items.description: La France et l’Italie se sont quittées sur un match nul (1-1), vendredi au Stade de France, à l’occasion de la troisième journée du groupe A1 de la Ligue des nations. Les Bleus, qui menaient au score, ont été rejoints en seconde période par une équipe italienne revenue dans la partie après une erreur défensive. Après une première période sans but, la France a pris l’avantage peu après la pause. Michael Olise a trouvé la faille sur une action consécutive à un coup franc, avec une frappe qui a terminé sa course sous la barre du but italien, ne laissant aucune chance à Gianluigi Donnarumma. Les Français ont ensuite eu plusieurs occasions de faire le break, mais le gardien italien s’est notamment illustré face à Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé et Eduardo Camavinga. La domination française ne s’est toutefois pas concrétisée par un deuxième but. L’Italie a finalement égalisé à la 68e minute. Alessandro Bastoni a profité d’une perte de balle française lors d’une relance pour récupérer le ballon, avancer et tromper Mike Maignan. Les Italiens ont ainsi ramené le score à 1-1. La fin de rencontre a été marquée par l’expulsion de Dayot Upamecano. Le défenseur français a reçu un deuxième carton jaune dans les dernières minutes, laissant les Bleus à dix pour la fin du match. Malgré cette infériorité numérique, les deux équipes n’ont pas réussi à se départager. Ce résultat permet à la France de conserver la tête du groupe A1 avec sept points, devant la Belgique, qui compte six unités après sa victoire contre la Turquie (3-0). L’Italie occupe la troisième place avec quatre points, tandis que la Turquie reste sans point. Cette rencontre constituait également le premier match de Zinédine Zidane à domicile à la tête de l’équipe de France. Le sélectionneur français avait auparavant remporté ses deux premières rencontres contre la Turquie et la Belgique sur le même score de 1-0. Dans l’autre rencontre du groupe, la Belgique s’est imposée 3-0 face à la Turquie grâce notamment à un doublé de Kevin De Bruyne et à un but de Romelu Lukaku.

items.title: Kankan : L’absence de défilé au cœur des regrets des citoyens lors de la fête de l’Indépendance
items.description: La Guinée a célébré, ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, le 68ᵉ anniversaire de son indépendance. À Kankan, deuxième capitale du pays, les festivités se sont déroulées à la place des Martyrs, en présence des autorités locales, des citoyens et de plusieurs acteurs de la vie publique. La cérémonie a été marquée par le dépôt de la gerbe de fleurs au monument dédié aux martyrs de la liberté, suivi des discours en hommage aux acteurs de l’indépendance de la Guinée, proclamée le 2 octobre 1958. Si la cérémonie s’est déroulée dans le calme, l’absence de défilé, autrefois considéré comme l’un des moments forts des célébrations du 2 octobre, a particulièrement retenu l’attention des citoyens rencontrés sur place. Pour plusieurs participants, le défilé contribuait à donner davantage d’animation et d’attractivité à la fête nationale dans les villes de l’intérieur du pays. « La fête s’est bien passée, sans problème. Mais il y a certaines anciennes choses qu’on commence à abandonner, notamment le défilé. Nous sommes venus pour la fête, mais il n’y a pas eu de défilé, alors que c’est cela qui donnait du goût à la fête du 2 octobre. Lors des défilés, on pouvait voir plusieurs démonstrations traditionnelles. Aujourd’hui, on vient simplement faire une promenade avant de rentrer », déplore Mamadi Camara, citoyen de Kankan. Même constat chez Amara Kanté, qui estime que l’absence de défilé a contribué à une mobilisation moins importante. « Les années précédentes, on faisait des défilés et les gens venaient de partout. Mais comme cette année il n’y en a pas eu, beaucoup de personnes n’ont pas eu la même curiosité de venir à la place des Martyrs. Nous sommes très contents de célébrer la fête de l’Indépendance. Certains qui étaient là l’année passée ne sont pas présents cette année. Nous prions pour le repos de leur âme et souhaitons une bonne santé au président » , témoigne-t-il. Pour Tady Camara, l’ambiance était également moins importante que lors des précédentes célébrations. « Je suis venue pour la fête de l’Indépendance, mais je ne vois pas beaucoup de monde et il n’y a pas autant d’ambiance que les années passées. Je souhaite que le président Mamadi Doumbouya vienne pour le 69ᵉ anniversaire de l’Indépendance afin que les gens viennent nombreux », souhaite-t-elle. Samboudjan Condé regrette, lui aussi, la disparition progressive du défilé dans les célébrations à l’intérieur du pays. « Nous voulons tous que la fête se passe très bien. Mais le manquement, c’est le défilé. Depuis que nous sommes petits, nous avons toujours vu cela. Aujourd’hui, cette tradition a perdu de l’ampleur et cela ne nous plaît pas. On ne peut pas dire qu’il n’y avait pas de monde, mais la mobilisation que nous connaissions auparavant n’était pas au rendez-vous. Beaucoup préfèrent aujourd’hui regarder à la télévision les défilés organisés à Conakry plutôt que de venir ici sans défilé », explique-t-il. Au-delà de l’aspect festif, l’absence de défilé semble également avoir eu des répercussions sur certaines activités commerciales autour du lieu de célébration. Aïcha Marega, vendeuse d’aliments, dit avoir constaté une faible activité commerciale au cours de la journée. « La fête de l’année passée ne m’a pas trouvée ici, mais je participe toujours aux événements pour vendre. Aujourd’hui, ça ne marche pas. Toutes les vendeuses sont assises. Je ne sais pas si c’est à cause de la situation économique ou parce qu’on est vendred i », explique-t-elle. Cette faible affluence est ainsi perçue par certains commerçants comme un manque à gagner, alors que les grandes cérémonies nationales constituent habituellement des occasions importantes pour les petits vendeurs. Malgré ces critiques et les regrets exprimés autour de l’absence de défilé, la célébration du 68ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance s’est déroulée dans le calme à Kankan. Aucun incident majeur n’a été signalé au cours de la cérémonie. Pour plusieurs citoyens rencontrés, l’enjeu est désormais de savoir si le défilé, longtemps associé aux célébrations du 2 octobre dans les villes de l’intérieur du pays, sera réintroduit lors des prochaines commémorations.

items.title: SSNIT says La Beach clearance was to protect hotel investments, beaches to remain public
items.description: The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has explained its decision to seek the removal of structures and unauthorised occupants from the beachfront adjoining the Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel in Accra. The clarification follows a demolition exercise on Friday, October 2, which affected several structures and businesses along the La Beach area, including La Pleasure Beach and Polo Beach Club. The operation, involving personnel from the 48 Engineer Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces and the Ghana Police Service, began in the early hours of Friday, with security personnel directing workers, traders, residents and operators to vacate the area. Several structures were subsequently demolished or partially pulled down. In a statement issued on Friday, SSNIT said it had sought the urgent intervention of the National Security Council Secretariat to address what it described as the “persistent unlawful occupation, encroachment, and unauthorised activities” on the beachfront adjoining and directly in front of the two hotels. SSNIT said the Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel form part of its investment portfolio and constitute significant national hospitality and tourism assets. It said it therefore had a fiduciary responsibility to protect the investments, preserve their value and ensure that they continued to generate sustainable returns for contributors and pensioners under the Basic National Social Security Scheme. “These assets belong to the workers and pensioners of Ghana,” SSNIT stated. Why SSNIT sought National Security intervention According to SSNIT, the continued encroachment on the beachfront presented a number of risks to the hotels and their operations. The Trust cited concerns about the safety and security of hotel guests, employees, service providers and visitors, as well as unauthorised access and proximity to sensitive guest and operational areas. It also identified increased exposure to fire, sanitation, environmental and public-health hazards as among the concerns associated with the continued occupation of the beachfront. SSNIT said the situation had also affected the condition of the beachfront, the privacy of the hotels and the service standards expected of internationally recognised hospitality facilities. It further raised concerns about the degradation of the coastal ecosystem, particularly as a result of construction activities on the beachfront and beach sand. The Trust said the situation could also cause reputational damage to the hotels, SSNIT and Ghana’s tourism industry. Another concern, it said, was the potential disruption of hotel operations and the guest beach experience, which could adversely affect patronage, revenue and the hotels’ overall financial performance. SSNIT also cited the risk that further expansion of the encroachments could make recovery of the affected areas increasingly difficult and costly. “In view of the foregoing, SSNIT requested support from National Security to protect the assets belonging to Ghanaian workers,” the statement said. Demolition not part of flood mitigation exercise The demolition initially generated questions about whether it formed part of the Government’s ongoing flood mitigation operations in parts of Accra. Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations, Stan Dogbe, subsequently clarified that Friday’s action was separate from the Government’s flood mitigation exercise. He said the operation was carried out under the supervision of National Security at the request of the Labadi Beach Hotel. Mr Dogbe said the structures affected, including the Polo Beach Club and other permanent structures, were located on the beach in front of the hotel and, according to the hotel, were affecting its safety, tranquillity and reputation, while diminishing the visitor experience. He also distinguished the exercise from the work of the Government’s National Flood Mitigation Task Force at locations including the Kpeshie Lagoon, East Legon Boundary Road, Oyarifa and behind Mayfair Estates. Mr Dogbe said there were also broader sanitation and security concerns associated with unauthorised and unregulated commercial activities along the beachfront. Beachfront to remain open to public SSNIT said the exercise was not intended to prevent the public from accessing the beach. It said the affected areas would be cleaned and restored to a safe and desirable condition. “The beaches will be cleaned and restored to a safe and desirable state and will remain open to the public,” the Trust stated. SSNIT did not, in the statement, announce plans to convert the cleared beachfront into a private facility or restrict public access. Rather, it said its intervention was aimed at protecting the hotels and the underlying investments while addressing the issues it had identified on the beachfront. Concerns over impact of demolition The exercise has, however, affected a number of businesses and workers operating in the area. The La Dadekotopon MP, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, confronted military personnel at La Pleasure Beach and questioned the basis for the exercise. She said she had engaged authorities over the planned demolition and had been assured that structures around the Labadi Beach Hotel would not be affected. Some operators also complained about the destruction of their businesses and property, with affected workers seen salvaging belongings from demolished structures. The demolition also followed earlier clearance activities in parts of the La Beach area, including structures at Laboma Beach. However, officials have stressed that Friday’s operation near the Labadi Beach Hotel should not be conflated with the Government’s separate flood mitigation programme. SSNIT’s latest statement, dated October 2, was issued by its Board of Trustees.

items.title: APSU congratulates St Augustine’s College after back-to-back National Investment Quiz wins
items.description: The APSU Secretariat has congratulated the St Augustine’s College team for successfully defending the National Investment Quiz trophy, following its victory in the 2026 competition. In a statement, the Secretariat described the back-to-back victories in 2025 and 2026 as a source of pride, noting that the National Investment Quiz plays an important role in building financial literacy among senior high school students and inspiring future leaders in Finance, Economics and Business. The Secretariat commended the contestants, coordinators, Steering Committee, College Management and staff for their hard work and contributions to the team’s success. It also expressed appreciation to APSUnians worldwide for what it described as their “unflinching support” throughout the competition. The 2026 grand finale featured four schools — St Augustine’s College, Mfantsipim School, Prempeh College and Corpus Christi Senior High School — in a closely contested battle that went down to the final rounds. Mfantsipim School made the strongest start, taking an early lead with 12 points in the opening round, while Prempeh College and Augusco had 10 points each. Corpus Christi had 5 points. Augusco responded in the second round, moving into the lead with 19 points, just one point ahead of Mfantsipim, while Prempeh College had 16 and Corpus Christi 11. The competition remained tight in the third round, with Corpus Christi and Prempeh College each scoring 13 out of 15. Mfantsipim and Augusco were also closely matched, recording 14 points each. The fourth round eventually gave Augusco some breathing room as the defending champions moved to 40 points. Mfantsipim followed with 36, Prempeh College had 33 and Corpus Christi finished the round on 23. The riddle round produced some of the most tense moments of the contest, with all four schools missing the first riddle after buzzing in. Corpus Christi then correctly answered the second riddle, before Augusco took the third and fourth. Mfantsipim answered the fifth and final riddle correctly, but Augusco’s consistency across the competition had already given the defending champions the advantage needed to retain the trophy. In a statement following the victory, the APSU Secretariat said it was “very gratified” by the college’s back-to-back success in 2025 and 2026. The Secretariat described the National Investment Quiz as an annual competition that builds financial literacy among senior high school students and inspires future leaders in Finance, Economics and Business. It expressed appreciation to the contestants, coordinators, Steering Committee, College Management and staff for their contributions to the victory. The Secretariat also thanked APSUnians around the world for what it described as their “unflinching support” for the team. The competition, which focuses on investment and financial literacy, has given students an opportunity to demonstrate their understanding of areas including stocks, bonds and investment fundamentals in a competitive setting.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : La SONATUR apporte 3 millions de FCFA à des structures sanitaire et éducative de Dogona
items.description: Dans le cadre de sa politique de responsabilité sociétale d’entreprise, la Société nationale d’aménagement des terrains urbains (SONATUR) a apporté, ce 2 octobre 2026, un soutien financier de 3 millions de francs CFA au Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de la trame d’accueil de Dogona et à l’école primaire publique du même quartier. La délégation a également visité plusieurs chantiers de la société à Bindougousso, dont celui des résidences Dafra. Conduite par le ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, Mikaïlou Sidibé, la délégation a entamé sa tournée au CSPS de la trame d’accueil de Dogona. Après avoir salué l’engagement du personnel soignant, elle a remis un chèque de 2 millions de francs CFA à la structure afin de soutenir son fonctionnement. La deuxième étape a concerné l’école primaire publique de Dogona. À cette occasion, la délégation a procédé à la pose de la première pierre du mur de clôture de l’établissement, au lancement des travaux de réalisation d’un forage et à la remise d’un chèque d’un million de francs CFA. « Toutes ces actions rentrent dans notre politique sociale d’entreprise. On a d’abord équipé le CSPS de matériel et de médicaments. L’école aussi, nous avons équipé de matériel éducatif dès leurs ouvertures. Aujourd’hui, nous sommes là encore pour les accompagner pour leur permettre de mieux fonctionner encore », a indiqué le directeur général de la SONATUR, Boureima Ouattara. Ces appuis s’inscrivent dans la volonté de la société d’accompagner les structures de proximité et de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations de la zone. 66 villas en construction aux résidences Dafra Après les actions de solidarité à Dogona, la délégation a visité plusieurs chantiers de la SONATUR dans le quartier Bindougousso. Au menu de cette tournée figuraient les travaux de voirie et d’assainissement, la construction du mur de clôture du cimetière du quartier ainsi que le chantier de la Cité SONATUR. Cette cité abrite les résidences Dafra, un programme immobilier composé de villas extensibles. « La cité SONATUR, ce sont des villas extensibles. C’est la première phase du vaste programme immobilier que la SONATUR va développer ici. Ce sont les résidences Dafra qui sont construites ici » , a expliqué le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé. Pour cette première phase, 66 villas sont en construction. Selon les informations communiquées lors de la visite, le taux d’exécution du chantier dépasse 75 %. Le ministre a salué les efforts des ouvriers mobilisés sur le site et les a invités à maintenir la cadence afin de garantir la qualité des ouvrages et le respect des délais. Avec ces initiatives sociales et ses projets d’aménagement urbain, la SONATUR poursuit ses interventions à Bobo-Dioulasso, entre accompagnement des services sociaux et développement de nouvelles offres immobilières. items.title: One feared dead in Aguleri, Umuoba Anam clash
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — One person was feared dead and several others injured following a fresh communal clash between Amaeze Aguleri and Umuoba Anam communities in Anambra East Local Government Area of Anambra State. Several buildings, including a microfinance bank in Aguleri, were reportedly set ablaze during the violence. The latest incident is believed to be linked to a longstanding land dispute between the two communities, which dates back to 1999 and had previously attracted the intervention of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. Accounts surrounding the dispute indicate that Amaeze Aguleri had decades ago given a portion of its land to Umuoba Anam on trust. The ownership of the disputed area later became a source of disagreement between the communities. The Anambra State Police Command confirmed the death of one person and said it had deployed personnel to the affected communities to restore peace and maintain law and order. The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Ama, led the state Deputy Governor, Dr Onyekachukwu Ibezim, other government officials, security agencies and community stakeholders on an on-the-spot assessment of the affected areas. The visit was aimed at assessing the security situation, safeguarding lives and property and preventing further escalation of the conflict. The delegation assessed the extent of the reported destruction and the impact of the violence on residents and the affected communities. The stakeholders also reviewed immediate measures to restore peace and strengthen security, while exploring longer-term steps to prevent a recurrence. During the assessment, Oji Ama reiterated the commitment of the Police Command to protecting lives and property and ensuring that residents could carry out their legitimate activities without fear. He urged residents of Aguleri and Umuoba Anam to remain calm and refrain from actions capable of escalating the situation. The police commissioner also appealed to residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could assist ongoing investigations and peace-building efforts. Speaking during the visit, Deputy Governor Ibezim urged traditional rulers, community leaders, youth organisations, town unions and other stakeholders to work with the government and security agencies towards finding a lasting solution to the dispute. He said security was a shared responsibility requiring the cooperation and commitment of all stakeholders. The Police Command assured residents of Aguleri and Umuoba Anam that security measures were being strengthened in the affected areas to prevent further breaches of peace. It added that efforts were ongoing to address the underlying issues through dialogue and other lawful channels. items.title: My experience with EFCC after my tenure as CBN governor – Soludo
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has recounted his experience with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) following the end of his tenure as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), saying the commission eventually cleared him of any wrongdoing in an investigation involving the Nigeria Security Printing and Minting Plc. Soludo spoke on Friday during the commissioning of the EFCC Awka Zonal Directorate Complex, which will serve Anambra and Imo states. The governor said he was invited for questioning after his name was mentioned in connection with an EFCC investigation into the activities of the Mint, where he had served as chairman of the board. He said he appeared before the commission after receiving a month’s notice of the investigation but did not hear from the EFCC for about a year. According to Soludo, he subsequently wrote to the commission seeking an update and was informed that the investigation had not established any corrupt conduct on his part. “My personal testimonies about the professionalism of this Commission is that when I left office as CBN Governor, EFCC was investigating Nigeria Printing and Minting Company, the Mint, an agency within the bank. “I was chairman of board of the Mint and was given one month notice of investigation and I showed up. After about a year, I didn’t hear from them, so I wrote them and they said that the investigation didn’t show any corrupt action about me,” he said. Soludo further said the then EFCC chairman had clarified that he was not the subject of the investigation after his name was mentioned in connection with the matter. He said the commission subsequently wrote to him confirming that its investigation had not established any wrongdoing on his part. “When my name was mentioned in connection with the investigation, the former chairman of EFCC told them that I was not the subject of the investigation. “Subsequently, the Commission wrote me a beautiful letter and said the investigation showed I didn’t have anything to do with the matter,” Soludo said. The governor said his experience had reinforced his appreciation of the commission’s work, particularly the need for investigators to formally communicate the outcome of inquiries to persons who were invited but not found culpable. “So I deeply appreciate the professionalism of the Commission. I want to urge that if you invite someone and later fail to find him complicit, you must write and say so, especially in this part of the world where, if you invite people, it finds its way into the pages of newspapers because they see invitation as an indictment,” he said. On the establishment of the EFCC’s Awka Zonal Directorate, Soludo said the state was pleased to host the facility, saying its presence would facilitate faster investigation of financial crimes in the region. “Some people might be asking why we are so excited about having the zonal office in our state. The reason for our excitement is that it will enhance quicker investigation,” he said. The governor said the EFCC’s staffing constraints made it difficult for the commission to establish offices in all 774 local government areas, adding that the Awka directorate would, in the meantime, serve Anambra and Imo states. “Ideally, EFCC should have offices in the 774 local government areas of the country, but with only about 6,000 staff, it is difficult to have offices in all LGAs. So this regional office will serve in the meantime and we will cooperate with you to serve the two states,” he said. Soludo said the Anambra State Government would seek the commission’s assistance in areas relating to revenue and taxation, while also working to improve knowledge of financial crime prevention among civil servants and local government officials. “We will not just be waiting for you to come from Abuja; we will be visiting you because it’s in our own interest that we should minimise financial crimes to the barest minimum. We assure EFCC of our fullest co-operation,” he said. He said the fight against economic and financial crimes required collective responsibility, assuring the commission that Anambra would cooperate with it in every possible way. According to him, the work of the EFCC was important to national development and required cooperation among government institutions and citizens. items.title: EFCC secures 1,370 convictions, recovers N1.23trn
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) secured 1,370 convictions from 1,889 cases filed in court during the first half of 2026, the commission’s Executive Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, has said. Olukoyede disclosed this on Thursday while speaking at the commissioning of the EFCC Awka Zonal Directorate Complex, which will serve Anambra and Imo states. He said the commission also recovered ₦1,233,612,040,411.11, $684,478,457.32, £373,905.78 and €9,343,803.66 during the period, in addition to recoveries in other currencies. Giving a broader account of the commission’s activities, Olukoyede said that between October 2023 and July 2026, the EFCC received 49,673 petitions, investigated 39,615 cases, filed 14,476 cases in court and secured 10,872 convictions. He said the figures represented a conviction-to-filing ratio of 75.1 per cent. According to him, the commission had introduced reforms aimed at improving its operations, including changes to its processes and procedures, which he said had contributed to its performance across various law-enforcement indicators. On the new Awka directorate, Olukoyede said its establishment was part of the EFCC’s expansion programme, supported by appropriations from the National Assembly and interventions by the Federal Government. He said Anambra and Imo required effective institutional presence because of their economic activities, describing the states as centres of enterprise, commerce and industry. Olukoyede said the EFCC’s mandate went beyond arrests and prosecution to include prevention and coordination in the fight against economic and financial crimes. “The EFCC exists not merely to arrest and prosecute. Our official mission encompasses prevention, enforcement and coordination in the effort to eradicate economic and financial crimes,” he said. He said preventing financial crimes before they occurred could help reduce the economic and social costs associated with fraud and diversion of public resources. “If we can identify vulnerabilities before billions of naira are lost, prevent fraudulent transactions before citizens lose their savings, strengthen procurement systems before public resources are diverted and interrupt criminal financial flows before they mature, then we would have saved the nation enormous economic and social costs,” he said. The EFCC chairman said the Awka directorate would place emphasis on corruption prevention and engagement with government institutions, businesses, financial institutions, professional bodies, schools, markets, civil society organisations, traditional institutions, religious bodies and communities. He urged members of the public to provide credible information about suspected economic and financial crimes, while cautioning against using whistleblowing to settle personal scores. “Whistleblowing must become an act of responsible citizenship,” Olukoyede said. “However, whistleblowing must be responsible and based on fact. It must not become an instrument for settling scores.” He called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, town unions, market associations, professional bodies, youth and women’s groups, civil society organisations and the media to support efforts to prevent corruption. Olukoyede also urged the new directorate to build sustained relationships with state and local governments, tertiary institutions, the organised private sector and community structures in Anambra and Imo. Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, said the commissioning reflected the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen the capacity of anti-corruption agencies. The President said his administration had, since assuming office, worked to improve the institutional capacity of anti-corruption agencies to carry out their mandates. He said the Awka directorate would strengthen the EFCC’s presence in Anambra and Imo, particularly in major commercial and industrial centres. “From the industrial towns of Onitsha and Nnewi, to the oil and gas town of Egbema and the rapidly growing economic city of Owerri, Imo State, the presence of EFCC will improve the ease of doing business,” Tinubu said. He said the government would continue to provide an enabling environment for anti-corruption agencies to carry out their responsibilities. Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, assured the commission of the state government’s cooperation in carrying out its duties. Soludo said reducing financial crimes was in the interest of the state and expressed satisfaction that Anambra would host the regional directorate. “Some people might be asking why we’re so excited about having the zonal office in our state. The reason for our excitement is that it will enhance quicker investigation,” he said. The governor, however, observed that the EFCC’s staffing capacity made it difficult for the commission to establish offices in every local government area. “Ideally, EFCC should have offices in the 774 local government areas of the country, but with only about 6,000 staff, it is difficult to have offices in all LGAs,” he said. Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, commended the EFCC for bringing its services closer to residents of the two states. Uzodinma also appealed to the commission to establish a dedicated state office in Imo to enhance its coverage and operations in the state. items.title: Abducted Corps Members: NANS raises alarm over ₦50m ransom
items.description: Demands review of long-distance NYSC postings By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Southwest Zone D, has raised concern over alleged ransom demands of up to ₦50 million for some prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted while travelling from Ibadan to their orientation camps. The association also called on the Federal Government to review compulsory long-distance postings and introduce safer deployment and transportation arrangements for prospective corps members. The demand followed the attack on two buses conveying prospective corps members and other passengers along the Owerri-Onitsha Road near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State. The Imo State Police Command confirmed that the buses were travelling from Ibadan to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, and Bende, Abia State, when they were attacked by suspected armed men. The police said 10 victims were rescued and both buses recovered, while the exact number of persons abducted was still being verified as security agencies continued search-and-rescue operations. In a statement jointly signed on Friday by NANS Southwest Zone D Coordinator, Adeyemo Josiah; General Secretary, Ojetola Babatunde; and Public Relations Officer, Olugbemi Timothy, the association described the incident as a serious security concern requiring urgent government action. NANS said information available to its leadership indicated that graduates from institutions in the South-West, including the Federal Polytechnic, Ede, and Osun State Polytechnic, Iree, were among those affected. The association expressed concern that the victims were travelling to comply with the compulsory national service programme, arguing that the government should take greater responsibility for the safety of graduates required to travel long distances for the programme. “A country cannot summon its youths and abandon their security,” the association said. On the alleged ransom demands, NANS said it had received reports and seen fundraising appeals suggesting that as much as ₦50 million was being demanded for each victim. It, however, urged security agencies and NYSC authorities to verify the reports and establish direct communication with the affected families before any conclusion was reached on the amounts allegedly being demanded. “If confirmed, it would be completely unacceptable for families whose children were kidnapped while travelling for national service to be left to crowd-fund tens of millions of naira to secure their freedom,” the association said. NANS also called for the immediate implementation of the risk-sensitive deployment framework approved by the Federal Executive Council in June 2026 as part of comprehensive reforms of the NYSC. The reforms approved by the FEC include a technology-driven call-up process, risk-sensitive deployment to improve the safety of corps members, a redesigned six-week orientation programme, skills-based primary assignments and improved orientation camp standards. The association argued that the latest incident underscored the need to move from policy approval to practical implementation of the safety measures. It also called for a review of compulsory long-distance interstate deployment and proposed state-based or zonal service options, particularly where security conditions make interstate travel difficult. “Until Nigeria’s security situation substantially improves, the Federal Government must seriously consider state-based and zonal service options, while making long-distance interstate deployment voluntary where circumstances justify it,” NANS said. “National integration remains important, but patriotism should never require a graduate to gamble with his or her life.” The students’ body further demanded organised and secured transportation arrangements for prospective corps members travelling to orientation camps. It proposed the use of accredited transport operators, designated travel corridors, vehicle-tracking systems and closer coordination between NYSC and security agencies during mobilisation periods. NANS also urged the authorities to review deployments to remote and high-risk communities and establish stronger emergency-response mechanisms for corps members serving across the country. The association disclosed that its Southwest leadership was reviewing more than 500 complaints and reports from students and graduates concerning the NYSC process. According to NANS, the complaints cover issues including delayed mobilisation, omissions from Senate and Academic Board lists, Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and institutional-record challenges, accreditation issues, registration and call-up difficulties, relocation, transportation, accommodation and reports concerning conditions in some orientation camps. It said the latest abduction had added an urgent security dimension to the administrative and welfare concerns surrounding the NYSC scheme. NANS called on the Federal Government, the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, NYSC management and security agencies to intensify rescue efforts until all remaining abducted persons were safely recovered. It also demanded verification of the reported ransom claims, direct official liaison with affected families and implementation of the approved risk-sensitive deployment framework. Other demands included a review of compulsory interstate deployment, consideration of state-based and zonal service options where necessary, secured transportation for prospective corps members and attention to outstanding mobilisation and welfare complaints. The association urged the Ministry of Youth Development, NYSC management and student representatives to convene an engagement on the security and welfare of prospective and serving corps members. Appealing to President Bola Tinubu, NANS called for urgent intervention in the incident, saying the government should ensure the safe recovery of the victims and take steps to prevent similar incidents. “When young Nigerians answering a compulsory Federal Government call are abducted on their way to orientation camp, while their families reportedly begin searching for enormous sums of money for their release, government cannot afford silence or delayed intervention,” it said. The association said the incident had generated anxiety among students, graduates and affected families, urging the government to provide clear updates on rescue efforts. NANS clarified, however, that while its Southwest leadership was responsible for raising concerns and escalating issues through the appropriate structures, any broader national decision or course of action remained the responsibility of the national leadership of the association. Reiterating its call for a comprehensive review of the NYSC scheme, the association said the security, economic and technological circumstances facing Nigerian graduates had changed considerably since the programme was established in 1973. “Nigeria in 2026 is not Nigeria in 1973 when NYSC was established. The country’s security realities, economy, technology and circumstances confronting graduates have changed, and NYSC must evolve accordingly,” it said. “We will not accept kidnapping as an unavoidable price of national service. We will not accept preventable danger as patriotism, and we will not normalise administrative hardship simply because the scheme has existed for decades.” The association expressed solidarity with the families of the affected prospective corps members and urged security agencies to sustain search-and-rescue operations until all victims were reunited with their families. “National service must never become national endangerment,” NANS said. items.title: Over 250 PDP, Accord members defect to APC in Oyo
items.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — More than 250 members and chieftains of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party have defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The defectors were received by the Oyo State leadership of the APC, led by its chairman and former Deputy Governor, Moses Alake Adeyemo, during a reception held at Watershed, Old Ife Road, Ibadan, on Friday. Addressing the new members, Adeyemo assured them of full integration into the party, saying they would not be discriminated against or denied equal participation in the affairs of the party. He said the APC was gaining support in the state amid what he described as dissatisfaction with the administration of the state government, adding that the party was positioned to provide an alternative in the 2027 election. According to him, “The people of Oyo State are tired of the maladministration of the APM, hence their desire for a change.” “APC remains the only party that can produce the required change in 2027. You have made the right decision. I am assuring you that you will not regret your action.” Also speaking, the APC governorship candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, outlined some of the policies he said his administration would pursue if elected governor in 2027. Alli said his proposed administration would prioritise education and healthcare, as well as review the state’s security architecture to address kidnapping, banditry and other security challenges. He said, “Our government will revamp the education, health and other sectors of the economy. “We are going to rejig the security architecture to bring an end to the reported cases of kidnapping, banditry and other vices in the past seven and half years. “There will also be a civil service reform with the training and retraining of workers. “Also, our administration will revisit the issue of the Circular Road that has left thousands of people homeless. “The local government autonomy will be the topmost priority of our administration.” Alli also pledged to pursue civil service reforms through continuous training and retraining of workers and review issues surrounding the Circular Road project. He identified local government autonomy as another priority of his proposed administration. Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Hon. Olamiposi Ojo, popularly known as Bibire Forum, who led members from Accord, said their decision to join the APC was based on what he described as the party’s commitment to internal democracy. Ojo also cited the leadership of President Bola Tinubu and what he described as the President’s impact on the country as factors behind their decision. He said, “Our decision is based on the leadership quality of President Bola Tinubu and the way he has been able to transform the country.” Similarly, Taoheed Ademola Lucky described the defection as a “homecoming” and expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects ahead of the 2027 elections. He pledged that his supporters would mobilise and work for the success of the APC at both the state and federal levels in the forthcoming elections. The post Over 250 PDP, Accord members defect to APC in Oyo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ASUU rejects Taraba committee on tertiary staff pay
items.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University (TSU) chapter, has rejected the constitution of a fresh committee by the Taraba State Government to review staff remuneration and workforce in tertiary institutions. The union described the move as unnecessary and capable of further delaying the implementation of an agreed salary structure for university workers. ASUU-TSU Branch Chairperson, Comrade Garba Mbave Joshua, stated the union’s position on Friday, October 2, 2026, at a press conference held at the union’s secretariat in Jalingo. Mbave said the government’s decision to constitute another committee was coming after several verification, consultation, financial computation and reporting processes had already been concluded by government and union representatives. He said the union had been negotiating the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government of Nigeria/ASUU Agreement with the state government since February 2026. According to him, TSU remained the only university in the 19 northern states yet to implement the agreed remuneration framework. Mbave said a government-backed verification team had earlier visited tertiary institutions across the six North-East states and submitted its report on September 22. He said the report established that neighbouring states had implemented the agreed salary table without variations. Following the verification exercise, he said, a tripartite committee comprising relevant stakeholders was constituted to determine the financial implications and accumulated arrears. The committee, according to him, submitted its final report to the Ministry of Tertiary Education on September 24. Mbave said the government, during a meeting on September 24, appealed to the union to suspend the industrial action it had contemplated following the expiration of its ultimatum. He said the appeal was reinforced by a formal request from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service for an additional two weeks to resolve the outstanding issues. According to him, the union subsequently convened its members on September 29 and agreed to grant the government the additional time requested in the interest of industrial harmony. “Notwithstanding the frustration and legitimate disappointment expressed by our members, Congress, acting in good faith and in the prevailing interest of industrial harmony, nevertheless acceded to the Government’s request and resolved to grant the Government the additional time sought,” he said. Mbave said TSU was among the institutions that had obtained approval to embark on industrial action but remained the only one that did not do so because the union decided to honour the government’s appeal for more time. He, however, said the constitution of another review committee had raised concerns among members because it followed processes that the union considered already concluded. “The constitution of yet another review committee, following the conclusion of the verification, consultation, negotiation, financial computation and reporting processes, gives rise to a legitimate and serious concern that the process is being subjected to further avoidable and unjustifiable delay,” he said. The union chairman said members viewed the latest development as potentially frustrating the implementation of the agreed remuneration framework. He reiterated that, to the best of the union’s knowledge, TSU remained the only university within the 19 northern states yet to implement the remuneration framework arising from the 2025 Federal Government/ASUU Agreement. ASUU-TSU therefore called on the state government to proceed with implementation of the agreed remuneration framework, settle accumulated arrears and give effect to the outcomes of the verification and tripartite processes already concluded. The union also urged the government to honour the assurances and commitments it made when requesting additional time to resolve the matter. items.title: The Right’s Identity Politics Takes a Bizarre Turn
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. If you want a snapshot of how the right has changed over the past decade, here’s one data point: MAGA activists think Sarah Huckabee Sanders is too woke now. That’s the same Sarah Huckabee Sanders who is the daughter of the GOP fixture Mike Huckabee and a former White House press secretary for President Trump. Now governor of Arkansas, she’s facing criticism from right-wing influencers over an ad boosting the state’s imposition of work requirements for recipients of the state’s Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act. These requirements are a long-standing Republican priority, but my colleague Annie Lowrey wrote last year that they are “a terrible idea” : The requirement creates new taxpayer costs and red tape without really solving any problem, because most Medicaid recipients who are physically able to work already do. That’s not why the activists are mad, though. They’re upset because the face of loafing in Sanders’s ad is a cheese-ball-snarfing couch potato named Brad who is a young white man. The “Pizzagate” influencer Jack Posobiec labels it “ Antiwhite .” Sean Davis of The Federalist calls it part of decades-long, systematic discrimination against white men. The openly bigoted investor James Fishback , fresh off getting trounced in a GOP primary for governor of Florida, traveled to Little Rock this week to rail against the “ false and disgraceful ad .” Assessing the accuracy of a fictional character in an ad feels a little absurd, but for the record: More than 60 percent of Medicaid-expansion enrollees in Arkansas are white, and 18 percent are Black, according to The New York Times . (The state overall is about 75 percent white and 15 percent Black.) A little more than half are women. Sanders rebuffed criticism, writing , “Next thing you know they’ll say I should have used cookies instead of cheese balls.” The immediate and obsessive focus on a throwaway character in a 30-second ad is a lurid reminder of how identitarianism has become influential in segments of the American right, particularly young voters. This is a matter of how members of the movement understand politics, as well as how they attempt to communicate to the American public. For decades, the right—as well as some centrist Democrats, such as Bill Clinton—criticized progressives for embracing identity politics. They argued that a focus on demographic segments was divisive and unhelpful. Ronald Reagan preached that “a rising tide lifts all boats” (though in practice this often meant support for trickle-down policies that helped mostly the already-thriving) and called for “color-blind” policies (which also tended to result in worse outcomes for people of color). This impulse persists in some segments of the Republican Party, most notably in the jurisprudence of the Supreme Court, led by the former Reagan aide John Roberts . This didn’t mean that people on the right hesitated to use race as a political wedge. They just did it elliptically. The avatar of this strategy was Lee Atwater, an adviser to Reagan and George H. W. Bush, whose 1981 explanation was as vulgar as the impulses he courted. “You start out in 1954 by saying, ‘Nigger, nigger, nigger,’” he explained . “By 1968 you can’t say ‘nigger’—that hurts you, backfires. So you say stuff like, uh, ‘forced busing,’ ‘states’ rights,’ and all that stuff, and you’re getting so abstract. Now you’re talking about cutting taxes, and all these things you’re talking about are totally economic things and a by-product of them is, Blacks get hurt worse than whites.” In 1980, for example, Reagan delivered a controversial speech at the Neshoba County Fair in Mississippi, not far from where the civil-rights workers James Chaney, Andrew Goodman, and Michael Schwerner were murdered in 1964, and spoke about “states’ rights,” a phrase that segregationists had adopted. In 1988, a pro-Bush group aired a commercial that attacked his Democratic opponent, Michael Dukakis, for allowing a convicted criminal named Wlliam Horton furlough from prison, during which he nearly killed someone. The ad didn’t mention Horton’s race and didn’t need to; it included his mugshot and called him “Willie,” which Horton (among others) interpreted as a dog whistle. “It was created to play on racial stereotypes: big, ugly, dumb, violent, Black—‘Willie,’” he said later. And, perhaps most relevant to the “Brad” brouhaha, Reagan often spoke about someone who became known as the “welfare queen.” As the journalist Josh Levin has written , this referred to a real individual, a woman in Chicago named Linda Taylor. Reagan never talked about her race, yet “welfare queen” became entrenched as a trope of lazy Black women grifting off the welfare system. This may explain why people such as Posobiec and Fishback are so agitated about the Arkansas ad: They understand how powerful a political weapon racial associations can be in shaping policy. But they don’t have Atwater’s finesse or plausible deniability. The right has gone from insisting that its rhetoric about entitlements was color-blind to demanding that it include racial signifiers. And though the number of Americans willing to tolerate or embrace gutter racism in politics appears to be growing, it remains a marginal group. The hardest-core activists, hyping one another up in group chats and on Discord servers, may have lost sight of that, failing to recognize how bizarre they look freaking out over a forgettable advertisement. If these identitarians looked around, they could see cautionary tales about the wholesale embrace of identity politics, such as the impression among many voters that the Democratic Party is more interested in niche groups than in ordinary people. They could learn from the first wave of the MAGA movement, which was willing to accommodate racism and bigotry for electoral gain but apparently believed that they could be contained and channeled. The commentator Erick Erickson, for example, has spent years tolerating Trumpism but now reacts with horror at neo-Nazis in the movement. Or they could consider the plight of Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who defended Trump’s every move from the White House lectern and now finds herself accused of treachery by his zealous followers. Related: James Fishback is an unsettling glimpse into the GOP’s future. The cynical Republican plan to cut Medicaid Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Exclusive: Is there anything Kash Patel won’t do for Trump before the midterms? Here’s who Democrats want to impeach next. The college decision just got harder. Today’s News New York Governor Kathy Hochul criticized Cornell University police and the local district attorney over their handling of a student’s 2024 rape allegations. Hochul appointed State Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to take over the reopened criminal investigation, which James said will include gathering evidence and interviewing witnesses while she considers whether to bring charges. The Kennedy Center Honors will be held outside the Kennedy Center for the first time in the ceremony’s history; it will take place in Washington’s Capital One Arena on December 7. The center’s main building has been closed since last month. President Trump is expected to name Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as the White House’s new AI czar , according to people familiar with the matter. Clayton would take on the role while continuing to oversee the nation’s intelligence agencies. Dispatches The Books Briefing : Robert Kolker’s The Vanishing Family joins a growing bookshelf of new works focused on dementia , Boris Kachka writes. Explore all of our newsletters here. Evening Read Illustration by The Atlantic. Source: Getty. The GOP’s Culture-War Hail Mary By Elaine Godfrey Last week, as the war with Iran dragged into its seventh month, gas prices shot up to an average of $4.50 a gallon, and polling showed President Trump about twice as far underwater with American voters as he was at this point in 2018, Republican senators determined that the time had come to discuss something else entirely: youth sports. “Girls’ sports are for girls. Boys’ sports are for boys,” Senator Marsha Blackburn said in a news conference. With 32 days to go until the midterm elections, Republicans’ closing strategy is obvious: They’re going all-in on trans. Read the full article. items.title: Culture : Dip Doundou Guiss dévoile « Yamay Gunguei
items.description: Le rappeur sénégalais Dip Doundou Guiss a dévoilé son nouveau clip intitulé « Yamay Gunguei », une production tournée intégralement dans le Sine Saloum et qui met en avant les paysages et le patrimoine naturel de cette région du Sénégal. Signifiant « c’est toi qui m’accompagnes » en wolof, « Yamay Gunguei » est une chanson d’amour dont le clip a été réalisé dans plusieurs sites du Sine Saloum, notamment à Palmarin, Fimela et Ndangane, ainsi que sur la route de Samba Dia. Le tournage s’est notamment déroulé aux Collines de Niassam, au Souimanga Lodge, sur le site des Aventuriers du Saloum chez Pierre et dans la Réserve naturelle communautaire de Palmarin. Dans ce nouveau projet, l’artiste associe son univers musical à la découverte des paysages de la région. Les mangroves, les lagunes, les pirogues et les couchers de soleil occupent une place importante dans les différentes séquences du clip. Le Sine Saloum y apparaît ainsi comme l’un des principaux éléments du récit. Conçu par Mahtarus et réalisé par Boubacar Woyo Traoré de Stick Production, le clip privilégie une esthétique basée sur la lumière naturelle et des plans contemplatifs. Ce choix permet de mettre l’accent sur les paysages et l’environnement du Saloum, en s’éloignant des décors urbains généralement associés aux productions de musique rap. Le projet bénéficie par ailleurs de l’accompagnement d’Africa Tourism Solutions, opérateur touristique associé à la valorisation de la destination Saloum, et de Samsung, partenaire technologique. Cette collaboration réunit ainsi des acteurs de la musique, du tourisme et de la technologie autour d’une même production culturelle. À travers ce clip, les promoteurs du projet souhaitent également contribuer à la visibilité du Sine Saloum, présenté comme un territoire disposant d’un important patrimoine naturel et touristique. La région, classée au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO, constitue l’un des principaux espaces de mangrove d’Afrique de l’Ouest. Le choix de Dip Doundou Guiss s’inscrit aussi dans la volonté de toucher un public jeune et la diaspora sénégalaise. L’artiste dispose d’une importante communauté au Sénégal et à l’étranger, notamment en France, en Italie et en Gambie. Disponible sur les plateformes et sur YouTube, « Yamay Gunguei » constitue ainsi une production musicale qui associe récit sentimental et mise en valeur d’un territoire sénégalais à travers l’image.
