items.title: Asagba Azinge at Two: Asaba sets new development pace
items.description: Opens anniversary with community-driven projects By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha ASABA — The Asagba of Asaba, His Royal Majesty, Prof. Epiphany Chigbogu Azinge, SAN, has said his two years on the throne have marked a shift from traditional rulership to a broader model of traditional governance focused on the welfare and development of the Asaba people. Azinge spoke on Monday as activities marking his second coronation anniversary began in Asaba, Delta State, with the unveiling and commissioning of several community-driven projects, including a smart nursery and primary school donated to the Delta State Government. Reflecting on his tenure, the monarch said he felt fulfilled by the support and participation of the Asaba community, stressing that leadership could not succeed without the active involvement of the people. “Leadership without followership is as good as dead. I draw a lot of strength and inspiration from the teeming number of Asaba people who have graciously donated their time, talent and treasure to whatever we have been doing,” he said. Azinge said his administration had deliberately expanded its focus beyond customs and traditions to address issues affecting the everyday lives of the people. “Like I’ve told many who care to listen, I’ve long migrated from being a traditional ruler, and I’m now into traditional governance. “Hence, I’m not only trying to think about the customs and traditions of our people; I’m also thinking about the welfare, healthcare, education, among so many other things, to make sure that my people are happy,” he said. Community donates smart school A major highlight of the anniversary was the commissioning and handover of the Smart Nursery and Primary School built by the Asaba community and donated to the Delta State Government. Azinge described the project as a demonstration of community participation in education and a commitment to complementing government efforts. He said the project was particularly significant because the community had not only built the school but decided to hand it over to the state government for use. “I believe in the history of Delta State, and I dare say in the history of Nigeria, today is the first time that a community will come together, not just to build a smart school, but also to have it donated to the state government,” he said. According to him, the project was initially funded through the community’s welfare fund before additional resources were mobilised to complete it. He commended the project supervisor for helping to mobilise additional funds after the community had exhausted its initial resources. Azinge also highlighted the facilities provided at the school, saying the community paid particular attention to the quality and suitability of the furniture. He said some of the specially designed chairs and tables cost about N100,000 each, with more than 80 units expected to be available for the school. However, while handing over the facility, the monarch appealed to the Delta State Government to provide an access road to the school. “If Asaba can donate a school to you, please donate a road to us so that we can achieve this. Donate a road so that people can access this place easily and then be able to school here,” he said. Delta lauds community partnership Representing the state government, the Commissioner for Primary Education, Chief (Mrs) Rose Ezewu, commended the Asaba community for the initiative. Ezewu described the project as an example of community participation and partnership in advancing education. “This occasion is significant not merely because we are unveiling a new school facility, but because we are witnessing the power of community vision, responsible leadership and purposeful partnership in advancing the cause of education,” she said. The commissioner said the government recognised that it could not meet every educational need alone and required collaboration with communities, traditional institutions, parents and other stakeholders. She assured the Asagba and the people of Asaba that the facility would be integrated into the state’s basic education system and managed in line with the educational needs of the pupils. More projects unveiled Other projects unveiled during the anniversary activities included a community cemetery, the beautification of Ogbeke Square, upgrading of Kanebisi Roundabout, formerly known as Traffic Light Junction, facilitated by Providus Bank, and a 1,000-capacity event centre at the permanent Asaba Palace grounds. Azinge said the projects formed part of a broader development vision for Asaba, adding that more projects were in the pipeline. “This is just a tip of the iceberg. I know that going forward, like I’ve promised, we are going to return here, and it’s going to be a totally new, transformed Ogbe-Ogo with all that everybody can think about,” he said. The monarch also announced plans to end burial activities within the community, saying a final proclamation would be made by December after further consultations with the Asaba-in-Council. Azinge said the anniversary was ultimately an opportunity to celebrate the collective spirit and unity of the Asaba people. “The support, the commonality of the things we do in Asaba is something that excites me, because once we voice it out, every other person supports, and that is not something that I want us to take for granted,” he said. The post Asagba Azinge at Two: Asaba sets new development pace appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Renewed flood intervention at Mallam Junction raises hopes among residents, businesses
items.description: Renewed government intervention at Mallam Junction is raising hopes among residents, motorists and businesses of a lasting solution to the recurring flooding that has affected the area. The latest efforts form part of a broader government response to the landfill, drainage and environmental challenges blamed for worsening flooding in Mallam and surrounding communities. The government has deployed personnel and operational teams to the Mallam area as part of efforts to address the underlying causes of flooding and improve the flow of stormwater. The intervention follows earlier engagements initiated from Jubilee House under the leadership of Chief of Staff Julius Debrah, bringing together relevant government agencies, the Weija-Gbawe Municipal Assembly and private-sector stakeholders operating around the affected area. Those engagements focused on the landfill, blocked drainage channels and other environmental factors associated with the recurring flooding around Mallam Junction. The renewed activity comes against the background of ongoing government efforts to restore waterways and drainage systems in flood-prone areas across Greater Accra. In August, work began to reclaim the Lafa water retention basin at Mallam, with the 48 Engineer Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces deployed to remove years of accumulated solid waste and silt that had reduced the basin’s capacity to retain stormwater. The operation also included the removal of illegal structures and plans to construct protective embankments. The Post-Flood Mitigation Task Force, which is coordinating the wider exercise, has said the objective is to restore the integrity of waterways and reduce the impact of flooding in affected communities. For residents and businesses around Mallam Junction, the renewed attention is being viewed as a welcome departure from interventions that often intensify only after heavy rainfall causes flooding. They say sustained government presence at the landfill and drainage sites could help address the conditions that contribute to the accumulation of floodwater, rather than relying solely on emergency responses after downpours. The Weija-Gbawe Municipal Assembly’s involvement is also considered critical, given its role in local sanitation enforcement, drainage maintenance and monitoring of activities around the affected areas. The Assembly has previously acknowledged the environmental challenges associated with the landfill, while residents have repeatedly raised concerns about waste dumping and blocked drainage channels in the area. Among businesses operating in the area, CAITECH has also expressed willingness to support efforts to address the flooding challenge, including providing funding, equipment and logistics for dredging and other remedial works. The renewed intervention therefore provides an opportunity for government agencies, the Municipal Assembly and private-sector operators to build on those commitments and pursue a coordinated response. Mallam Junction has repeatedly experienced flooding during periods of intense rainfall, affecting traffic movement, businesses and residents in surrounding communities. The wider Lafa basin has also been identified as a critical part of the flooding challenge. Officials from the Ghana Hydrological Authority have explained that years of dumping, siltation and encroachment had significantly reduced its capacity to receive and channel stormwater. The government’s current approach seeks to address those underlying conditions through dredging, waste removal, drainage works and enforcement against encroachment. For commuters who regularly use the Mallam corridor, sustained improvements in drainage and waste management could help reduce disruptions to traffic and access to surrounding communities. Businesses also stand to benefit from a cleaner and safer environment, particularly as flooding along major commercial and transport corridors can disrupt operations, damage property and affect customer access. Residents are consequently calling for the current momentum to be maintained until the landfill, drainage and wider environmental challenges are comprehensively addressed. They say the immediate objective is not simply to clear floodwater after heavy rains, but to address the conditions that cause or worsen flooding in the first place. The renewed activity has also placed greater emphasis on collaboration between central government, the Weija-Gbawe Municipal Assembly and businesses operating around Mallam. Such cooperation, residents say, will be important in preventing illegal dumping, maintaining drainage channels and ensuring that activities around the area do not further obstruct the natural flow of stormwater. The current intervention has therefore shifted attention towards how the government and other stakeholders can sustain the work and translate the ongoing operations into a more permanent solution. For many residents, the priority is straightforward: they want an end to the recurring flooding that has disrupted their lives, businesses and daily movement. The renewed deployment of personnel and equipment to the Mallam area has consequently been welcomed as a positive development, with residents hopeful that the combined efforts of government agencies, the Post-Flood Mitigation Task Force, the Weija-Gbawe Municipal Assembly and private-sector stakeholders will produce lasting results. What residents now want is continuity—ensuring that the work continues beyond the immediate operation until the landfill, drainage and environmental challenges around Mallam Junction are durably addressed.

items.title: Tunisie | Sahbi Atig en grève de la faim depuis mardi dernier
items.description: Privé d'un parloir spécial, le dirigeant du parti islamiste Ennahdha, Sahbi Atig, a entamé une grève de la faim depuis mardi dernier, annonce son épouse Zeineb Mraihi. Dans une vidéo publiée ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026 après une visite à la prison, Zeineb Mraihi a précisé que son époux a décidé de maintenir la grève de la faim jusqu'à ce qu'il puisse obtenir un parloir spécial (visite directe et sans barrières). Il a par ailleurs affirmé que si son état de santé venait à se dégrader, il refuserait de se rendre à l'hôpital, tout en soulignant que son seul souhait est d'obtenir son droit, a ajouté son épouse, sans cacher son inquiétude quant à l'état de santé de son mari. Elle a de ce fait rappelé que Sahbi Atig, âgé de 67 ans, avait observé en juillet 2023 une grève de la faim qui avait duré 54 jours pour protester contre ce qu’il considère comme une détention injuste et injustifiée, et que cela avait impacté sa santé, désormais fragilisée, a-t-elle souligné. Mme Atig rappelle par ailleurs que son mari a fait l'objet de jugements le condamnant à une peine totale de 23 ans : « Il lui reste 20 ans de prison… On a appris à prendre notre mal en patience et tout ce qu'on demande, c'est qu'il les passe au moins dans la dignité et qu'il jouisse de ses droits . ». Y. N. L’article Tunisie | Sahbi Atig en grève de la faim depuis mardi dernier est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Le général qui n'a pas demandé la permission
items.description: Avril 1994. Pendant que les grandes puissances négociaient leur retrait du Rwanda en flammes et que l'ONU comptait ses pertes, un général ghanéen prenait une décision que personne ne lui avait demandé de prendre. Il n'a pas appelé Accra. Il n'a pas attendu les ordres. Il n'a reçu aucune garantie. Il a regardé un peuple en train de mourir, et il a dit : nous restons. Trente mille personnes sont en vie grâce à ces deux mots. Nous sommes en avril 1994. Le Rwanda brûle. Pas métaphoriquement. Les collines sont en feu. La radio (Radio Mille Collines) ordonne aux hommes hutu de saisir leurs machettes et d'achever le travail. « Coupez les grands arbres », dit-elle. Tout le monde sait ce que cela signifie. Les Tutsi sont les grands arbres. Ils étaient traqués et assassinés systématiquement ; des Hutu opposés aux massacres étaient également tués. Et le monde, qui observe de loin, a décidé qu'il en a assez vu. Le 21 avril, le Conseil de sécurité des Nations Unies vote la réduction de sa force de maintien de la paix au Rwanda. L'UNAMIR devait être réduite de quelque 2 500 soldats à seulement 270. La Belgique s'est déjà retirée : dix de ses soldats ont été torturés et assassinés dès le premier jour, leurs corps mutilés, et Bruxelles a décidé qu'elle n'avait plus d'appétit pour cela. Le Bangladesh part. Les Tunisiens font leurs bagages. D'autres pays évacuaient leurs ressortissants. L'ordre tombe : préparez le retrait. Dans le compound de l'ONU à Kigali, le général canadien Roméo Dallaire—l'homme qui avait alerté le monde six mois plus tôt, qui avait envoyé le désormais tristement célèbre « fax du génocide » à New York en suppliant qu'on lui permette d'agir, à qui on avait répondu de ne rien faire—se tourne vers son adjoint. Le général de division Henry Kwami Anyidoho. Né à Tanyigbe, au Ghana. Cinquante-trois ans. Soldat depuis 1965. Un homme qui avait servi au Liban, au Liberia, au Cambodge. Un homme qui avait assez vu le monde pour savoir exactement ce qui se passait ici, et exactement ce que signifierait partir. Et il allait devoir répondre à une question pour laquelle aucune école militaire ne prépare vraiment un homme : Que reste-t-il de votre devoir lorsque presque tout ce qui devait vous permettre de l'accomplir disparaît ? Dallaire lui demanda ce que les Ghanéens allaient faire. Anyidoho n'hésita pas. « Je n'avais même pas demandé la permission à Accra quand je lui ai dit que nous resterions », dira-t-il plus tard. « Nous n'avions pas le choix. Nous ne pouvions pas abandonner ces gens. » Il le dit simplement, de la façon dont un homme dit quelque chose qu'il a déjà décidé au fond de lui-même : Nous ne partons pas. Comprenez ce que cette décision a coûté. Le contingent ghanéen était arrivé au Rwanda avec 850 soldats. Désormais, après les retraits successifs, Anyidoho en gardait 454—pour la plupart de jeunes hommes, à peine sortis de l'entraînement, envoyés par leur pays pour maintenir une paix qui n'existait plus. Ils étaient en infériorité numérique. Ils étaient sous-équipés. Les Interahamwe avaient des machettes, des grenades et une station de radio qui leur disait que Dieu voulait cela. Les Ghanéens avaient des fusils, des munitions insuffisantes et un mandat que l'ONU venait d'annuler de facto. Et ils restèrent. Ils transformèrent le stade Amahoro en sanctuaire. Des milliers de Tutsi et de Hutu modérés se déversèrent par ses portes — des familles, des enfants, des personnes âgées, des gens qui avaient marché pendant des jours à travers des barrages routiers où la mauvaise réponse à une seule question signifiait la mort. Les Ghanéens se tenaient en périphérie. Ils négociaient. Ils bluffaient. Ils utilisaient leurs corps comme seule barrière entre les vivants et les hommes qui voulaient les tuer. La situation logistique était si désespérée que le seul avion-cargo canadien assurant les rotations vers Kigali atterrissait, déchargeait sa cargaison en roulant, et redécollait sans s'arrêter. Il n'y avait pas le temps de s'arrêter. Et pourtant, les Ghanéens restèrent. Quelques semaines après le début des massacres, un autre officier ghanéen, le colonel Clayton Boanubah Yaache, reçut une mission. Il fallait évacuer environ 80 personnes, identifiées comme Tutsi ou Hutu modérés, qui s'étaient réfugiées à l'Hôtel des Mille Collines (l'hôtel qui deviendrait plus tard célèbre comme décor du film Hôtel Rwanda). Yaache les avait dissimulés dans des camions bâchés, et il avait passé des jours en réunion avec les commandants Interahamwe, négociant l'autorisation pour le convoi. Il l'avait obtenue…sur le papier. Au cinquième barrage après l'hôtel, le papier ne valait plus rien. Six cents miliciens crevèrent les pneus de ses camions. Ils arrachèrent les bâches. Ils regardèrent les gens à l'intérieur et les appelèrent inyenzi — cafards — et annoncèrent qu'ils les tueraient tous. Avec des grenades. Avec des machettes. Avec leurs mains s'il le fallait. Yaache n'avait pas d'arme. Ses dix soldats n'avaient pas la puissance de feu suffisante pour affronter six cents hommes. Il n'y avait pas de cavalerie en route. Pas de soutien aérien. Personne au bout d'une radio qui pouvait sauver ces gens. Il n'y avait que lui. Et sa voix. Et douze heures. Il exigea qu'ils appellent leurs commandants. Il alla et vint, heure après heure, tandis que le soleil traversait le ciel et que les gens dans les camions attendaient en silence, sachant. Les miliciens retiraient les goupilles des grenades et les tenaient devant son visage. Il ramassait les goupilles et les remettait en place. Il continuait à parler. Il ne fuyait pas. Il ne suppliait pas. Il négociait — avec le calme implacable d'un homme qui avait décidé que ces quatre-vingts personnes allaient vivre, et que c'était simplement la fin de l'histoire. Quand le soleil se coucha enfin, douze heures après le début, un chef adjoint des Interahamwe intervint. Les camions furent autorisés à repartir. Les quatre-vingts personnes vécurent. « Bien des fois, nous étions impuissants », dira Yaache plus tard, sa voix portant le poids de tout ce qu'il avait vu. « Tu vois l'homme le faire, et tu ne peux rien faire. Tu cries avec ta bouche, c'est tout. » Mais ce jour-là, sa bouche suffit. Quand Anyidoho rentra au Ghana, le président Jerry John Rawlings—lui-même militaire, un homme que rien n'émeut facilement—le convoqua. Rawlings était en colère. Ou quelque chose d'approchant. Il demanda à Anyidoho : que devais-je dire à ce pays si tous nos soldats avaient été tués ? Anyidoho réfléchit. Puis il dit : « Monsieur le Président, il y a certaines choses dans la vie qui sont inexplicables. Nous étions dans une situation où nous devions agir selon les impératifs de notre conscience. » Il marqua une pause. « Que nous ne mourions pas — que nous ne perdions pas trop de soldats dans ces circonstances — cela ne pouvait être qu'un acte de Dieu. » Cinq Ghanéens furent tués ou blessés. Selon l'estimation de Dallaire lui-même, le contingent contribua à sauver peut-être 30 000 vies. Trente mille. En juillet 2022, le président Paul Kagame décerna à Anyidoho et au général de division Joseph Narh Adinkra l'Ordre national du courage du Rwanda — l'Indengabaganizi. Debout devant eux, Kagame déclara : « Un génocide ne produit pas de héros. Simplement faire son devoir a exigé un courage exceptionnel. Là où d'autres ont fui ou ont été rappelés par leurs gouvernements, abandonnant les Rwandais à leur sort, ces officiers sont restés et ont continué à diriger leurs hommes et leurs femmes, et ont fait ce qu'il fallait faire. La plupart ont échoué à l'épreuve. Ces officiers, non. » En juin 2026, le Rwanda a érigé deux monuments permanents à Burma Camp, à Accra—l'un pour les plus d'un million de victimes du Génocide contre les Tutsi de 1994, l'autre pour les soldats de la paix ghanéens qui ont refusé de partir. Ce sont les premiers monuments de ce type érigés dans un pays africain qui n'a pas ses propres victimes. Le Rwanda les a construits quand même. Parce que certaines dettes ne peuvent pas être remboursées. Elles ne peuvent qu'être rappelées. Jack Parnell était là. Il l'a vu. « Le professionnalisme accompli, la discipline, le courage et le dévouement dont a fait preuve chaque soldat de la paix sous la direction d'Anyidoho », a-t-il écrit récemment. « Leur conduite était exemplaire. » Saviour Anyidoho—le fils du général—a écrit : « Mon père et les troupes nous ont laissé un héritage de service désintéressé et le mandat de ne jamais nous laisser aller à un tel endroit à nouveau. » Marcel Shyaka, survivant du Génocide contre les Tutsi, l'a dit simplement : « Leur courage et les vies qu'ils ont protégées méritent d'être reconnus. » Dallaire l'a dit le mieux. Il le dit toujours. « L'épine dorsale de tout cela—ma capacité à rester et à faire quoi que ce soit—était due aux Ghanéens et au général Anyidoho qui sont restés. Les autres ont fui, tandis que les Ghanéens sont restés. » Le monde a un mot pour ce qui s'est passé au Rwanda en 1994 : échec. Un million de Tutsi assassinés en cent jours. Le génocide le plus efficace de l'histoire moderne. Une catastrophe que le monde a vue venir, dont il a été averti, et qu'il a choisi de ne pas arrêter. Mais à l'intérieur de cet échec, il y a une histoire plus petite. L'histoire de 454 jeunes hommes d'un pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest qui ont regardé l'ordre de partir et ont dit non. Qui ont transformé des stades en sanctuaires. Qui se sont tenus à des barrages routiers avec pour seule arme leur voix. Qui ont ramassé des goupilles de grenades par terre et les ont remises en place. Qui sont restés. Trente-deux ans plus tard, le président Paul Kagame parlera des « blessures invisibles » que les soldats avaient rapportées avec eux. Il a raison. Henry Kwami Anyidoho a 86 ans. Il vit au Ghana. Il ne mange toujours pas facilement de la viande ; il lui a fallu des années après le Rwanda pour recommencer, car la viande lui rappelait ce qu'il avait vu au Rwanda. Certaines choses, on les porte pour toujours. Mais trente mille personnes sont en vie parce qu'il a pris une décision dans un compound de l'ONU à Kigali en avril 1994, sans demander la permission, sans attendre les ordres, sans savoir s'il en sortirait vivant. Nous ne partons pas. Quatre mots. Plus de trente mille vies. Voilà à quoi ressemble le moment où une personne décide que l'histoire n'aura pas le dernier mot. ━━━━━━━━━ Envie de lire mes prochaines histoires dès leur parution ? items.title: Nwifuru: Ebonyi, university to resolve pension crisis
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has said his administration is working with the management of the state university to resolve the dispute over the payment of pensions and gratuities owed some retired workers of the institution. Nwifuru spoke while responding to an appeal by more than 200 retirees who sought his intervention over the non-payment of their retirement benefits. The governor explained that the responsibility for employing workers of the university rested with the institution’s management, rather than directly with the state government, adding that the existing legal framework did not automatically make the state responsible for their retirement benefits. According to him, the key issue was determining the appropriate authority responsible for the payment of the affected workers’ pensions and gratuities. “The problem now is who actually is responsible for the payment of the pensions and gratuities of these people, since the government of Ebonyi is not the one employing them. They are not the ones hiring,” he said. Nwifuru said the state could not automatically assume responsibility for workers it did not employ, stressing that employment and termination responsibilities were linked. “The law is very clear. You cannot fire who you did not hire. That’s the problem that they are facing,” he said. The governor, however, said his administration had reached an understanding with the university management to accommodate the affected retirees and explore ways of addressing their concerns. “We have gotten to a point that we agreed with the management of the university. We agreed that what we should do is accommodate these people that are already crying,” he said. Nwifuru further explained that universities operated under different financial and administrative structures, with responsibility for workers’ pensions depending on the status and management structure of the institution. “If they are being run by government, it is the responsibility of government; their staff are staff of that state government. But if they are not being run by government, then you cannot say that the government should also pay,” he stated. He said the university management was working with relevant authorities to resolve the matter and develop a workable arrangement for the affected retirees. On infrastructure development, Nwifuru said work was progressing at the ICT University despite the state’s limited resources. The governor said his administration had deliberately reduced spending on elaborate project commissioning ceremonies and publicity, arguing that scarce public resources could be redirected to infrastructure development. “We are not spending much money in order to commission projects. We have small resources, so the money we would spend on television houses, media houses and social media for commissioning projects can be used to do one kilometre of road,” he said. Nwifuru also disclosed that President Bola Tinubu would commission projects at the ICT University, including the Senate building, during his planned visit to Ebonyi State. “We have Mr President. Anytime Mr President is coming here, he will commission that project,” he said, adding that another project would also be commissioned during the visit without disclosing details. items.title: Belgium’s De Bruyne fires double to sink Turkey, France held by Italy
items.description: Kevin De Bruyne scored twice as Belgium beat Turkey 3-0, while France were held 1-1 by Italy in the Nations League on Friday. Napoli midfielder De Bruyne, in his 127th match for the Belgians, scored the opening goal, playing a nice one-two with Dodi Lukebakio before a cool finish from the edge of the box. While Belgium looked threatening without creating many clear-cut chances, Turkey posed the greater attacking danger after De Bruyne’s opener. But they had no reward for their efforts in the Belgian city of Liege. Instead, De Bruyne claimed a second, curling a ball from the edge of the box past Turkey goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir into the top corner. A third came from Romelu Lukaku, Belgium’s all-time record goalscorer, who had replaced Lukebakio. A low cross from Charles De Ketelaere fell to Lukaku, who managed to skew the ball past Cakir from close range. It was a third defeat in as many games for Turkey, while the result left Belgium one point adrift of Group A1 leaders France. Zinedane Zidane’s French team took the lead through Michael Olise in the 55th minute. But Alessandro Bastoni equalised to deny Zidane victory in his first home game in the dugout for France. A two-match winning run comes to an end, too, after Les Bleus concede for the first time under the World Cup winner. Veteran striker Robert Lewandowski scored a hat-trick as Poland thrashed Romania 6-0 in Group 4 of League B, which also saw Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sweden battle to a 1-1 draw. Ciaron Brown scored twice as Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 3-0 on neutral territory in Trnava, Slovakia, while Hungary beat Georgia 1-0 in the other Group 2 match. Earlier in League C, Cyprus beat Armenia 2-0 at home in Group 2, while Montenegro managed a 2-1 win over Latvia in Riga. In Group 3 action, Moldova pipped Kazakhstan 2-1 in Astana, while the Faroe Islands snagged a 1-1 home draw with Slovakia. The post Belgium’s De Bruyne fires double to sink Turkey, France held by Italy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le PI prépare son entrée dans le futur gouvernement conduit par le PAM
items.description: Le Parti de l'Istiqlal s'achemine résolument vers une reconduction de sa présence au sein du futur gouvernement, dont la conduite a été confiée par le Roi Mohammed VI à Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, Cheffe du gouvernement désignée et coordinatrice du Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM). Les délibérations au sein du Comité exécutif de la formation historique traduisent une volonté claire d'inscrire cette démarche dans la continuité directe des urnes, l'Istiqlal ayant décroché la troisième place lors des récentes élections législatives avec un bloc solide de 66 sièges à la Chambre des représentants. Une session cruciale du Conseil national du parti doit se tenir ce week-end afin d'analyser en profondeur les enseignements du scrutin, de valider officiellement l'orientation fixée par la direction et de mandater ses représentants pour la suite des négociations. Cette mobilisation istiqlalienne repose sur la conviction profonde que la participation aux affaires publiques constitue le prolongement naturel et responsable des grands chantiers sociaux et économiques engagés sous la précédente législature. La direction PI entend ainsi maintenir l’empreinte de sa référence politique égalitaire et son identité doctrinale spécifique, tout en apportant son expertise technique et politique à l'action gouvernementale à venir. Parmi les priorités stratégiques majeures mises en avant figure le dossier de l'intégrité territoriale et le déploiement opérationnel du plan d'autonomie dans les provinces du Sud. Dans ces régions sahariennes, le parti centenaire bénéficie d'un ancrage sociopolitique, tribal et électoral historique, de nature à renforcer considérablement la légitimité et l'efficacité des politiques publiques locales. Dans sa conduite des discussions, la direction du parti de la balance a fait le choix délibéré de ne poser aucun préalable rigide ni d'imposer de veto à l'égard des autres acteurs du paysage politique national, écartant ainsi d’emblée tout risque de blocage institutionnel ou de crise négociationnelle. Les échanges internes au sein du Comité exécutif se sont concentrés sur les grands axes doctrinaux de la participation plutôt que sur la distribution prématurée des portefeuilles ministériels, un volet qui sera arbitré dans un second temps, une fois le feu vert formellement accordé par le parlement du parti. Interrogée sur la perspective de reformer l'alliance tripartite ayant réuni le PAM, le RNI et l'Istiqlal durant le précédent mandat, la direction invoque la carte de « l'intérêt national » pour surmonter les vives frictions verbales et les joutes électorales inhérentes à la campagne. Estimant avoir mené une campagne sereine, mesurée et dénuée d'invectives, l'Istiqlal considère sa démarche en parfaite adéquation avec la position affichée par le Rassemblement National des Indépendants. Ce dernier s'est également dit prêt à contribuer activement à la future majorité, dessinant ainsi les contours d'une coalition gouvernementale stable, structurée et armée pour faire face aux défis économiques, sociaux et géopolitiques majeurs de la période actuelle. © Mounir Mehimdate Cette convergence stratégique entre les trois plus grandes forces politiques du pays ouvre la voie à une transition institutionnelle fluide, propre à rassurer les acteurs économiques et la scène internationale. En privilégiant la stabilité exécutive et le pragmatisme politique, le Parti de l'Istiqlal cherche à s'imposer comme un garant de l'équilibre au sein de la nouvelle majorité. Cette posture vise à aborder les échéances cruciales à venir, notamment les grandes réformes structurelles, la consolidation de l'État social et la préparation des grands rendez-vous internationaux du Royaume, avec un exécutif fort et doté d'une assise parlementaire confortable. The post Le PI prépare son entrée dans le futur gouvernement conduit par le PAM appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Two suspected cultists killed in Osogbo shooting
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo OSOGBO — Two suspected members of a cult group were reportedly killed during a suspected cult clash in Osogbo, Osun State capital, on Friday evening. The incident occurred at a lounge around Owoeba, in the Owode-Ilesa Garage area of the city, causing panic among residents and forcing some business owners to shut their shops. Sources said a rival group stormed the lounge where one Adebayo Taoreed, popularly known as Small Rugged, and other persons were relaxing and opened fire. Taoreed was said to have been linked to the Eiye cult group, although the claim could not be independently verified. Another person, identified only as OSHA, was also reportedly killed, while four others sustained gunshot injuries. The shooting triggered panic along the Ilesa Garage-Ayepe axis as gunmen allegedly fired sporadically while fleeing the scene. Some residents and traders reportedly ran for safety, while business owners hurriedly closed their shops to avoid being caught in the violence. Confirming the incident, the Osun State Police Command spokesperson, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, said the command was aware of the shooting, which he described as a suspected cult clash. Ojelabi said two persons were killed at the scene, identifying one of them as Small Rugged, while the identity of the second victim had yet to be established. According to him, four other persons sustained gunshot injuries and were taken by the police to a nearby hospital for treatment. “The command is aware of a shooting incident suspected to be cult clash around Owoeba area, Osogbo. “Two persons died at the spot, one identified as Small Rugged, while the other’s name is yet unknown. “Four other people sustained gunshot injuries and have been rushed by the police to a nearby hospital for treatment,” he said. The police spokesperson added that the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, had directed tactical teams to apprehend those responsible for the shooting. Meanwhile, claims linking Taoreed to alleged thuggery and political violence during the 2026 Osun State governorship electioneering could not be independently verified. The police had not announced any arrest in connection with the incident as of the time of filing this report. The post Two suspected cultists killed in Osogbo shooting appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police repel bandits’ attack on Sokoto village
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Operatives of the Sokoto State Police Command have foiled an attempted attack by suspected bandits on Tsabre Village in Isa Local Government Area of the state, recovering two rocket launchers and two empty AK-47 magazines. The incident occurred at about 1am on Friday, October 2, 2026, when the armed men reportedly stormed the community and opened fire. The police said tactical teams responded to a distress call and engaged the attackers in a gun battle, forcing them to retreat into a nearby forest. According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufa’i, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Hayatu Hassan Shaffa, the Divisional Police Officer in Isa immediately mobilised the Anti-Kidnapping Unit and the Violent Crime Response Unit after receiving information about the attack. The statement said the tactical teams engaged the attackers in a prolonged gun battle and eventually forced them to flee. It added that the fleeing attackers reportedly sustained casualties, although the command did not disclose the number. Following the encounter, the police conducted a search of the surrounding bushes and recovered items allegedly abandoned by the attackers. They included two rocket launchers, two empty AK-47 magazines, a keypad Tecno phone without a battery, a touch light, an army jungle hat, a sweater cap, five pairs of sandals and a rain jacket. Commending the operatives, Shaffa praised their prompt response and determination to protect residents. He said the operation demonstrated the command’s resolve to prevent criminal elements from attacking communities across the state. “The Command remains resolute in its commitment to protecting the lives and property of the people of Sokoto State,” he said. The commissioner urged residents to remain vigilant and provide security agencies with credible information that could assist in preventing attacks and apprehending suspects. He also appealed to residents to report anyone suspected of sustaining gunshot injuries and seeking medical treatment to the nearest police station or other appropriate security authorities. The command assured residents that its tactical teams would sustain operations against banditry and other violent crimes, particularly around vulnerable communities in the state. items.title: St Augustine’s College retain National Investment Quiz title after nail-biting grand finale
items.description: Four schools walked into the grand finale of the 2026 National Investment Quiz, but only one walked out with the trophy, and it is the same school that lifted it last year. St Augustine’s College, known as Augusco, successfully defended the title, beating back stiff competition from Mfantsipim School, Prempeh College and Corpus Christi Senior High School in a contest that swung several times before the final whistle. The signs of a close fight showed from round one, where Mfantsipim (Botwe) took an early lead with 12 points, with Prempeh College and Augusco tied on 10 points and Corpus Christi trailing on 5. By round two, Augusco had surged ahead with 19 points, narrowly ahead of Mfantsipim’s 18, Prempeh’s 16 and Corpus Christi’s 11. Round three saw Corpus Christi and Prempeh College each post 13 out of 15, while Mfantsipim and Augusco matched each other with 14 out of 15, keeping the contest finely balanced heading into the final round. The fourth round proved decisive. Augusco pulled clear with 40 points, with Mfantsipim close behind on 36, Prempeh College on 33 and Corpus Christi on 23. The riddle round provided some of the evening’s tensest moments. All four schools buzzed in on the first riddle and got it wrong: Augusco, Mfantsipim, Prempeh College and Corpus Christi all missed their attempts in turn. Corpus Christi recovered to take the second riddle correctly, before Augusco answered the third. Augusco went on to take the fourth riddle as well, before Mfantsipim closed out the riddle round with the fifth and final correct answer. In the end, however, it was Augusco’s consistency across the quiz rounds that proved decisive, sealing their status as the first school to retain the National Investment Quiz title since the competition began. Mfantsipim School, Prempeh College and Corpus Christi Senior High School all put up spirited performances, and organisers say the standard of competition this year reflects just how far the quiz has grown since its inception. The 2026 National Investment Quiz, organised to deepen financial literacy among Senior High School students, has, over the years, turned subjects like stocks, bonds and investment basics into topics teenagers can confidently debate and defend on stage. Win or lose, every school on the platform this year leaves with financial lessons that will outlast the competition itself.

‘Nothing to show after 24 years in power’, Wike knocks Amaechi
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said his predecessor, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi, has nothing to show for 24 years as Speaker, Governor and Minister. He challenged the people of Evo Kingdom in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State to point to any tangible development or political empowerment Amaechi attracted to their land. According to a statement on Friday night by Lere Olayinka, his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, the minister spoke at an interactive session with leaders and stakeholders of Evo Kingdom. “Someone was Speaker of the House of Assembly for eight years, Governor for eight years, and Minister for eight years, that is 24 years in top leadership positions! What can anybody point to that he attracted to Evo Kingdom or Rivers State in all those 24 years? Nothing! Not one single thing!” Wike said. He drew a contrast with his own record. “I was a Minister of State for Education, and as I sit here, I can count the projects I brought to Rivers State and my people. But somebody was Speaker, Governor, and headed a very lucrative ministry as a full Minister for eight years, yet brought nothing back home! How can someone who spent 24 years in power without empowering his people or raising new leaders now turn around to tell you he loves you?” he asked. Wike also reiterated his decision to resign as Minister should President Bola Ahmed Tinubu lose in Rivers State and the FCT. He made the declaration at a strategic consultative meeting with stakeholders of Akpor Kingdom in Obio-Akpor on Friday, where he rallied the political structure of Rivers State behind the President. “My interest in Rivers State is for God to use me as a vessel to help our people. I am back here not for what I will get, but for what I will be to raise my people,” he said. He said politics was driven by the collective interest of the people and not by perpetual animosity. “There is no permanent enemy in politics; what we have is permanent collective interest. It is all about the interest of our people. The more you are in number, the happier you become. Leadership is like a waste dustbin. If you cannot absorb things, both the good and the bad, then you cannot be a true leader,” he said. Wike told political actors in the state not to be distracted by social media criticism of his open-door policy towards former detractors, saying true political strength lies in numbers. He demanded an all-inclusive campaign structure across Obio-Akpor. “Whether you are a politician, whether you are a traditional ruler, whether you are a pastor, or whether you are a native doctor, I need everybody now,” he said, adding: “For the purpose of voting and elections, we must bring everyone together.” The post ‘Nothing to show after 24 years in power’, Wike knocks Amaechi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Événements politico-judiciaires entre 2021 et 2024 : une enquête recense 76 décès et plus de 200 victimes présumées (Procureur)
items.description: Le Parquet du Tribunal de grande instance hors classe de Dakar a annoncé l’ouverture d’une enquête sur des faits présumés de torture, de traitements inhumains, cruels ou dégradants, ainsi que d’autres infractions susceptibles de recevoir la qualification de crimes contre l’humanité entre 2021 et 2024. Selon un communiqué du procureur de la République, les premières investigations ont permis de dénombrer provisoirement 76 personnes décédées et plus de 200 victimes présumées. L’enquête fait suite à deux correspondances, les numéros 559/MJ du 28 juillet 2025 et 0260/PGDK du 30 juillet 2025, par lesquelles le parquet a été saisi pour instruire des faits survenus entre 2021 et 2024. Le 4 août 2025, le chef d’escadron commandant la Section de recherches de la Gendarmerie nationale de Dakar a été saisi à cet effet. Menées entre octobre 2025 et septembre 2026, les premières investigations, fondées sur les documents disponibles, ont permis de recenser provisoirement 76 personnes décédées, dont 41 dans la région de Dakar, ainsi que plus de 200 autres victimes présumées d’actes de torture ou de traitements inhumains, cruels ou dégradants. Cinq personnes interpellées Les auditions des victimes et des témoins, ainsi que l’exploitation des actes médicaux, ont révélé des indices d’assassinats, de meurtres, de persécutions et d’actes de torture ou d’autres traitements inhumains, cruels ou dégradants, susceptibles de constituer des crimes contre l’humanité. Les investigations ont abouti à l’arrestation de cinq personnes. Quatre sont soupçonnées d’avoir participé à des actes de torture exercés sur Pape Abdoulaye Touré. La cinquième est mise en cause dans le décès de Mamadou Ndoye, que le communiqué présente comme ayant été volontairement heurté à mort par un véhicule de la Police à Bargny. Le 23 septembre 2026, les cinq personnes ont été inculpées pour crimes contre l’humanité, notamment pour des faits de torture et de meurtre, par les juges d’instruction co-saisis. À l’issue de cette procédure, deux d’entre elles ont été placées sous mandat de dépôt, tandis que les autres ont été soumises à des mesures de contrôle judiciaire ou à une assignation à résidence avec surveillance électronique, selon les modalités précisées par le communiqué. Le parquet fait appel de l’ordonnance Le 28 septembre 2026, le procureur de la République, qui avait requis le placement sous mandat de dépôt de l’ensemble des inculpés, a interjeté appel de l’ordonnance rendue par les juges d’instruction. Le communiqué indique également que les magistrats instructeurs ont été invités à établir les délégations judiciaires, à formuler les demandes de concours nécessaires, à délivrer les commissions rogatoires et à accomplir les autres actes d’instruction utiles à la manifestation de la vérité. Le parquet précise enfin que d’autres procédures judiciaires pourront être ouvertes devant les juridictions compétentes, en fonction des niveaux de responsabilité que l’enquête et l’instruction permettront d’établir. Les investigations se poursuivent donc afin de déterminer les responsabilités individuelles dans les faits examinés.

items.title: Inclusion sociale : Une ONG plaide pour l’autonomie des femmes handicapées
items.description: Dans le cadre du projet « Voix des femmes », l’Ong « Humanité et Inclusion » et ses partenaires mobilisent la société civile pour exiger la participation active des femmes et filles handicapées aux instances de décision et aux politiques publiques. L’Ong « Humanité et Inclusion » a organisé, hier, une session de plaidoyer multi-acteurs réunissant des organisations féministes, de défense des droits humains et des membres de la société civile. L’objectif est de porter le combat contre la faible présence des personnes handicapées, surtout les femmes et les filles, dans les programmes et politiques publiques, ainsi que dans les instances de décision. La rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Voix des femmes », mis en œuvre au Sénégal, au Togo et au Bénin par « Humanité et Inclusion ». À cette occasion, Françoise Gabriella Mballa, chargée de projet à « Humanité et Inclusion », a indiqué que des avancées sont notées dans la prise en charge du handicap au Sénégal, mais qu'il reste encore à faire. Selon elle, les filles et les femmes sont encore privées de certains de leurs droits. Ces couches vulnérables sont confrontées au problème d'accessibilité aux services sociaux de base, aux postes électifs, aux instances de décision, aux financements et à la participation citoyenne et politique. À cela s’ajoutent les violences basées sur le genre dont beaucoup de filles et femmes handicapées sont victimes. Dans le même sillage, les participants ont demandé la ratification du Protocole africain relatif aux droits des personnes handicapées, ainsi que la révision de la loi d'orientation sociale. « Les femmes et les filles handicapées ne doivent pas être seulement des bénéficiaires des politiques et programmes. Elles doivent pouvoir participer à leur conception, leur mise en œuvre, leur suivi et leur évaluation », a déclaré Isseu Gaye, présidente du Comité des femmes de la Fédération sénégalaise des associations de personnes handicapées. Le conseiller du président de la République chargé du handicap, Cheikh Saad Bou Diouf, partage cet avis. Selon lui, le temps est venu de passer définitivement d'une approche basée sur l'assistanat à une approche fondée sur les droits, l'égalité, l'autonomie et la pleine participation. « Une femme handicapée n'est pas seulement une personne à protéger, et le handicap ne doit jamais être une condamnation à l'invisibilité », a-t-il affirmé. items.title: Education infrastructure investment will drive Banda’s development – Ahmed Ibrahim
items.description: Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources and Member of Parliament for Banda, Ahmed Ibrahim, says the government’s investment in educational infrastructure is critical to developing the human capital needed to drive sustainable development in the district. According to him, the expansion and modernisation of facilities at Bandaman Senior High Technical School will equip young people with the scientific, technical and vocational skills required to take advantage of emerging opportunities, including those associated with major projects in the area. Speaking during an inspection of ongoing GETFund projects at the school, Mr Ibrahim said Banda must move beyond dependence on agriculture and deliberately invest in education and skills development. “We are in the era of knowledge capital, where the human resources of the place, of the people, are the greatest asset that we have,” he said. He explained that about 44,000 acres of land in the Banda District had been acquired for the construction of the Bui Hydro Dam project, affecting communities whose livelihoods are predominantly dependent on farming. Mr Ibrahim said the development made it even more important for residents to acquire the technical and scientific skills necessary to benefit from opportunities created by the project. He noted that although the Bui Power Authority employs about 644 workers, only a small number are from the district. “Clearly, if care is not taken to train the people scientifically, in the near future the sustainability of the project will not be guaranteed,” he added. Mr Ibrahim said this was the motivation behind prioritising secondary and technical education in the district, with a focus on science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM). He said the upgraded school would help produce electrical and mechanical engineers, doctors, accountants and other professionals capable of securing employment in major institutions and projects within the district and beyond. “Now that government is building a modern STEM science laboratory for us, we have no excuse. We just have to strengthen the basic education to make sure that we produce teachable children for the secondary school,” he said. The minister expressed confidence that the infrastructure investment could transform the school into one of the leading second-cycle institutions in the region. Bandaman Senior High Technical School, established in 2010, currently has a student population of 687. However, inadequate infrastructure, including an abandoned E-Block, has constrained teaching and learning. Headmaster Ebenezer Kofi Latah said the pressure on existing facilities has affected the school’s ability to provide a learner-centred environment. “The dining hall is just a small space, and now, looking at our population, sometimes during break time, we need to break them into two or three batches, and that is affecting instructional time,” he said. He added that the girls’ dormitory was also operating at full capacity. Under GETFund’s New Targeted Emergency Projects, nine major projects are being undertaken at the school. They include a 2,000-capacity dining hall and kitchen, two two-storey dormitory blocks for boys and girls, seven two-unit semi-detached teachers’ bungalows, a three-bedroom headmaster’s bungalow, a three-storey 18-unit classroom block, a two-storey science laboratory, a two-storey administration and library block, science laboratory equipment, boreholes and external works, including a gatehouse. Zonal Consultant of AESL for the Bono, Ahafo and Bono East regions, Simon Mawuli Sabakpo, said the projects were at various stages of completion. He said some of the teachers’ bungalows could be completed and handed over within a month, while contractors were working to complete the other facilities ahead of schedule. The headmaster said completion of the projects would significantly improve teaching and learning while allowing the school to admit more students. “With the science laboratory, I’m told that it’s going to be equipped and fully furnished. So the massive infrastructure development here is going to be a relief to our school,” Mr Latah said. “We really pray that the project will be completed on time, so that the school can admit more, and then it will facilitate teaching and learning.” The Acting President of the Banda Traditional Council, Nana Peh Aboatea II, also appealed to natives of Banda, both within and outside the district, to support efforts to improve educational infrastructure in the district.

items.title: 2027: Prepare for your resignation – NDC tells Wike
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) chapter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has asked the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to prepare his resignation, following his declaration that he would quit office if President Bola Tinubu loses the FCT and Rivers State in the 2027 presidential election. The NDC made the call on Thursday in Abuja while reacting to Wike’s declaration during an engagement with members of the Apo Mechanics and Traders Association on September 30. Wike had said he would announce his resignation as FCT Minister on January 17, 2027, if Tinubu failed to win the presidential election in both the FCT and Rivers State. “If I cannot deliver where I work, then I’m not worthy to be here. If I lose FCT, I’m not supposed to be FCT Minister. By January 17, 2027, I will announce my resignation as FCT Minister should the President lose in Rivers State and the FCT,” Wike said. Reacting, the NDC FCT Publicity Secretary, Prince Samuel Iloh, said Wike should begin preparing his resignation letter, arguing that the minister could not determine how FCT residents would vote. Iloh said eligible voters in the territory had the constitutional right to choose their preferred candidates at the polls, adding that the outcome of the election would be determined by voters. He also dismissed what he described as expectations that Wike’s political mobilisation would automatically translate into electoral victory for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the FCT. “If not that he is taking Nigeria as a banana republic, how could a politician be making such a claim when he has only one vote to cast for the President in Rivers and not even in the FCT?” he asked. The NDC spokesman urged FCT residents to participate actively in the January 16, 2027 presidential election and vote for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, with Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. He also called on voters to support the party’s National Assembly candidates in the territory, including Amanda Pam for the Senate, as well as Hassan Grema and Adamu Kamal for the House of Representatives. Iloh further challenged the APC to secure victory in the FCT, recalling that the party’s presidential candidate, Tinubu, came second in the territory in the 2023 presidential election. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi of the Labour Party won the FCT in 2023 with 281,717 votes, while Tinubu polled 90,902 votes and the Peoples Democratic Party’s Atiku Abubakar scored 74,194 votes. Iloh said the 2023 result was an indication of the voting pattern in the territory, but added that the outcome of the 2027 election would ultimately be determined by voters. He urged eligible residents to participate in the electoral process and protect their votes, while expressing confidence in the NDC’s candidates across the FCT. POESAM 2026 : Orange Maroc propulse trois innovations marocaines à fort impact vers la finale internationale
items.description: Agriculture durable, intelligence artificielle, emploi, cybersécurité, santé, éducation… La 16ᵉ édition du Prix Orange de l’Entrepreneur Social en Afrique et au Moyen-Orient (POESAM) confirme la vitalité d’une nouvelle génération d’entrepreneurs marocains qui mettent la technologie au service de problématiques concrètes. Avec 345 candidatures reçues à travers le Royaume, l’édition 2026 témoigne de la dynamique de l’entrepreneuriat à impact au Maroc. À travers le POESAM, Orange Maroc poursuit une ambition : faire émerger les talents, accélérer les solutions à fort potentiel et leur donner les moyens de changer d’échelle. Trois innovations marocaines distinguées À l’issue du processus de sélection, 14 startups finalistes ont présenté leurs projets devant un jury composé d’experts et de dirigeants d’Orange Maroc. Innovation, viabilité du modèle économique et impact sociétal ont constitué les principaux critères d’évaluation. Trois startups se sont distinguées : • 1er Prix National : AgroLora : une solution combinant IoT et intelligence artificielle pour assurer un suivi intelligent et durable des exploitations agricoles. • 2è Prix National : Invirtus : une plateforme de recrutement basée sur l’intelligence artificielle permettant d’évaluer les compétences réelles des candidats. • 3è Prix National : Arwa Solutions : une plateforme AgriTech mettant les agriculteurs en relation avec des conseillers IA afin d’optimiser leurs pratiques agricoles durables De la récompense à l’accélération Au-delà du prix, l’ambition d’Orange Maroc est d’accompagner ces entrepreneurs dans la durée. Les trois lauréats intégreront l’écosystème d’accompagnement d’Orange Digital Center et d’Orange Fab Maroc, avec l’accès à des expertises, des formations et des dispositifs d’accélération destinés à soutenir leur développement. Ils représenteront également le Maroc lors de la finale internationale du POESAM, ouvrant leurs projets à de nouvelles perspectives à l’échelle de l’Afrique et du Moyen-Orient. « Notre ambition n’est pas seulement de récompenser l’innovation marocaine, mais de lui donner les moyens de changer d’échelle. Ces entrepreneurs partent de réalités très concrètes du Maroc et mobilisent la technologie pour y apporter des réponses utiles. Le rôle d’Orange est précisément là : connecter les talents, la technologie et les opportunités pour faire émerger les solutions de demain » , souligne Hendrik Kasteel, Directeur Général d’Orange Maroc. Une nouvelle génération de Tech marocaine Au-delà des trois lauréats, cette édition met en lumière la diversité des usages développés par l’écosystème entrepreneurial marocain. Les startups finalistes interviennent notamment dans la santé avec Peren AI, l’éducation avec Bewize, l’économie circulaire avec Plakkar, la cybersécurité avec Radar Cyberone, la finance avec Akkan et Legalplus, ou encore la mobilité avec Venez. Cette diversité traduit une même dynamique : utiliser la technologie non comme une fin en soi, mais comme un levier pour répondre aux transformations économiques, sociales et environnementales du Royaume. À travers le POESAM, Orange Maroc entend ainsi contribuer à faire émerger une Tech marocaine utile, ambitieuse et capable de rayonner au-delà des frontières du Royaume. Parce qu’une innovation prend toute sa valeur lorsqu’elle passe de l’idée à l’impact. items.description: Says coordinator arrested while seeking release of colleague By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Obidient Movement has called for the release of its Akwa Ibom State Coordinator, Dr Ben Smith, and the State Coordinator of the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement, Elijah Noah, following their reported arrests during the controversy surrounding a planned Independence Day march in Uyo. The movement also criticised the decision by the Akwa Ibom State Police Command to stop political rallies, meetings and processions scheduled for October 1, describing the development as a restriction on political expression. The development followed a directive by the police command ordering political parties, groups and associations to reschedule activities earlier approved for the Independence Day date, citing security concerns. The command said it had intelligence suggesting that some individuals could exploit political gatherings to cause disturbances and threaten public peace. The planned “Two Million-Man March” was organised by supporters of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso. The Obidient Movement, in a statement signed by its Media and Communications Directorate, Onyeka Dike, said Smith was arrested after he went with other supporters to seek the release of Noah and other members who had earlier been detained. The movement demanded the immediate release of the two coordinators and other detained members. According to reports, Noah was arrested after security operatives moved to stop the planned march, while Smith was subsequently reported to have been taken into custody at Ikot Akpan Abia after accompanying supporters seeking Noah’s release. The movement alleged that the arrests amounted to intimidation of its members and called for an end to what it described as harassment of opposition supporters. It said, “The Obidient Movement strongly condemns the arrest of the Akwa Ibom State Coordinator of the Obidient Movement, Dr Ben Smith, the State Coordinator of the OK Movement, Mr Elijah Noah, and other members of the Obidient Movement by the Nigeria Police during a peaceful march yesterday. “Their simple offence was for identifying as Obidients, a fundamental human right guaranteed by the Nigerian Constitution.” The movement further said the arrests raised concerns about citizens’ rights to peaceful assembly and political expression. It called on the authorities to release the detained members and prevent the disagreement over the cancelled march from escalating. The group also warned that continued arrests could lead to wider protests, saying it might mobilise its members and supporters for demonstrations in other parts of the country. “If the authorities continue to ignore our demands and use the police to intimidate peaceful citizens, we will have no choice but to mobilise our members and supporters for wider protests around the country,” the statement said. The movement had earlier questioned the cancellation of the march, with Smith saying the organisers had spent more than N20 million on mobilisation, branding and logistics across the 31 local government areas of the state. The reported expenditure has been presented as the organisers’ claim. However, the police have maintained that the directive was not targeted at any particular political group. Commissioner of Police in Akwa Ibom State, Baba Mohammed Azare, said organisers of the march had attended a meeting with the command where they were advised to reschedule the event because of security concerns. The police also said the directive applied to political activities generally and that the decision was based on available security intelligence and concerns over public safety. The command further said those who proceeded with the march despite the directive were arrested for investigation and that persons found to have violated the directive could face legal action. The police position contrasts with the Obidient Movement’s account that the arrests were connected to peaceful political expression. The controversy has therefore shifted beyond the cancelled march to questions surrounding the regulation of political gatherings, the enforcement of police directives and the rights of political supporters to peaceful assembly ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Obidient Movement urged the authorities to resolve the matter and release those it said remained in custody, while calling for restraint by all parties involved. The post Uyo March Fallout: Obidient Movement demands release of detained coordinators appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Kogi Central APC stakeholders pledge support for Yahaya Bello
items.description: Ex-gov: ‘Kogi election is as good as done for APC’ KOGI — Former Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Yahaya Bello, on Friday received supporters and All Progressives Congress, APC, stakeholders in Kogi Central as he returned to the district ahead of the 2027 senatorial election. The homecoming attracted supporters from the five local government areas that make up Kogi Central, with party members gathering to welcome the former governor and APC senatorial candidate. Bello emerged as the APC candidate for Kogi Central Senatorial District after winning the party’s May 18, 2026 primary with 72,399 votes. Ibrahim Yakubu Adoke scored 319 votes, while Momoh Yusuf Obaro polled 188 votes. However, Bello’s emergence is being challenged in court by Obaro, who is seeking to nullify the primary result. The Federal High Court in Abuja has fixed November 19, 2026, for judgment in the matter. Speaking at the homecoming, former Kogi State APC Chairman and former Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Abdullahi Bello, described the turnout as a demonstration of support for the former governor. “This is the homecoming of a leader that liberated the whole Ebiraland, and we all trooped out to welcome him. It is not an easy thing. We love him and we have to demonstrate that,” he said. Abdullahi said APC members in Kogi Central were prepared for the 2027 election and expressed confidence in the party’s support base in the district. “I will not flatter you with words, but obviously, as you can see for yourself, Ebiraland, Kogi Central, is the home of the All Progressives Congress. APC is here. APC lives here. We preach APC,” he said. He added that APC members across the five local government areas would mobilise support for Bello. “APC is 100 per cent prepared to vote Alhaji Yahaya Adoza Bello to the Red Chamber come next year,” he said. The former chairman also attributed the support for Bello to what he described as achievements recorded during his tenure as governor, particularly in the areas of security and infrastructure. According to him, the district had experienced violent conflicts in the past, but he said the situation improved during Bello’s tenure. “Before now, especially 2007 and 2008, this Central used to be a battlefield, burning of houses and killing of innocent people. But the coming of Alhaji Yahaya Bello put an end to all that,” he said. Other constituents who spoke at the event also expressed support for the former governor and pledged to mobilise for his senatorial bid. Responding, Bello thanked the people for the reception, describing the turnout as “organic,” “inborn” and “inherent.” Speaking to journalists at the palace of the Ohinoyi of Ebira Land, Bello expressed confidence in the support of the people of Kogi Central for the APC and its candidates in the 2027 elections. “I have never doubted that my people are with me 100%. I have never doubted that my people are supporting APC 100%. I have never doubted that my people will support and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 100%. I have never doubted that my people are with my governor, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo 100%,” he said. On his senatorial ambition, Bello said he believed the people were aware of what he described as the APC’s contributions to infrastructure and development in the state. “I have never doubted that my people are going to vote myself as the senator representing Kogi Central and all of our other candidates on the platform of All Progressives Congress because they know very well what this party has done to liberate our people and bring infrastructure to the people and ensure that dividend of democracy is delivered to our people,” he said. Bello also expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the state, saying, “Kogi State is 100% APC and APC is Kogi State 100%.” He added: “I want to assure Mr President that Kogi State election is done and Kogi Central in particular is as good as done 100% for APC.” The homecoming marked a public show of support for Bello among APC stakeholders and supporters in Kogi Central as political activities ahead of the 2027 senatorial election intensify. The post 2027: Kogi Central APC stakeholders pledge support for Yahaya Bello appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Segundo día del temporal de lluvias torrenciales: Tarragona supera los 250 litros y Castellón los 170
items.description: España afronta el segundo día de azote del fuerte episodio de lluvias torrenciales, intensos chubascos y tormentas que continuará hasta el miércoles, pero la fase más adversa ha pasado ya. Al mediodía, tal y como estaba previsto, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) ha levantado los últimos avisos rojos que afectaban al sur de Tarragona y al litoral de Castellón . En puntos de la primera provincia se han superado los 250 litros de agua por metro cuadrado acumulados hasta esta mañana desde el jueves y, en la segunda, los 170. Según informa Rubén del Campo, portavoz de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) , la previsión es que por la tarde continúe la probabilidad de tormentas y chubascos muy fuertes en los litorales del sur de Cataluña, de la Comunidad Valenciana, en toda Murcia, Almería, Ibiza y Formentera, todos ellos bajo aviso naranja. Seguir leyendo ¿Por qué está lloviendo tanto si no hay una dana detrás? Lo que más está sorprendiendo a los expertos de la fase más adversa de este temporal es la ausencia de una gran estructura como culpable de semejante virulencia en las lluvias, que están siendo torrenciales y persistentes sin necesidad de que exista una dana o una borrasca o una vaguada que las provoque... Primero, la fuente de inestabilidad era un frente de una borrasca atlántica, después, había una débil vaguada atravesando la Península, elementos que, "por sí mismos, no justificarían las cantidades tan extraordinarias de precipitación", explica el veterano meteorólogo Ángel Rivera , que culpa a "la gran humedad disponible en capas bajas sobre el Mediterráneo a consecuencia de las altas temperaturas del verano". La Aemet también considera que una de las claves es la "temperatura del agua del mar" . Muchas zonas del Mediterráneo occidental superan los 26°, algo más propio de agosto. Son valores hasta 4° superiores a lo normal para estas fechas. "Un mar cálido provoca mayor inestabilidad por el contraste de temperatura entre el aire frío de las capas altas de la atmósfera y el templado y húmedo situado sobre la superficie del mar. Además, provee de mayor humedad a la atmósfera, al haber más evaporación en aguas cálidas", explica la Aemet. El meteorólogo de la agencia Benito Fuentes anota que esta "anomalía cálida del Mediterráneo es 100 veces más probable en un mundo con cambio climático", por lo que el causante último de lo ocurrido es el calentamiento global. Fuentes también recalca la ausencia de una dana, que en el imaginario colectivo se ha convertido en la única causa y sinónimo de lluvias torrenciales. "Los episodios de precipitación extrema no siempre van asociados a una dana. En esta ocasión, es por culpa del anticiclón, que configura un flujo marítimo en capas bajas, ayudado por bajas presiones en el norte de África, junto a otros factores", explica en X .

items.title: ONUDI-Japon : Echanges autour du développement industriel en Tunisie
items.description: Le Japon, premier contributeur gouvernemental au financement volontaire de l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour le développement industriel (ONUDI) en 2025, entretient avec l’Organisation un partenariat couvrant notamment le transfert de technologies et de compétences, le renforcement des capacités industrielles ainsi que l’appui aux entreprises et aux chaînes de valeur. Dans ce contexte, une rencontre s’est tenue entre S.E. M. SAITO Jun, Ambassadeur extraordinaire et plénipotentiaire du Japon en Tunisie, et M. Lassaad Ben Hassine, Représentant de l’ONUDI en Tunisie, accompagné de ses collègues Mme Giusy Musaro et M. Idriss Guerziz. Les échanges ont porté sur les activités de l’ONUDI en Tunisie et les priorités en matière de développement industriel durable et inclusif. La rencontre a permis de présenter le portefeuille de coopération technique de l’ONUDI en Tunisie ainsi que les principales orientations du futur Programme de Partenariat Pays (PCP) Tunisie 2026-2030, notamment en matière de compétitivité des PME, d’innovation et de transformation numérique, de transition énergétique et de décarbonation, d’économie circulaire et de développement des compétences. Ces priorités sont alignées sur le Plan de développement de la Tunisie 2026-2030 et s’inscrivent dans les orientations du Cadre de coopération des Nations Unies pour le développement durable (UNSDCF) 2027-2031. Communiqué L’article ONUDI-Japon : Echanges autour du développement industriel en Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: ‘Nothing to show after 24 years in power’, Wike knocks Amaechi.
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said his predecessor, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi, has done nothing to show for 24 years as Speaker, Governor and Minister. He challenged the people of Evo Kingdom in the Obio-Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State to point to any tangible development or political empowerment Amaechi attracted to their land. According to a statement on Friday night by Lere Olayinka, his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, the minister spoke at an interactive session with leaders and stakeholders of Evo Kingdom. “Someone was speaker of the House of Assembly for eight years, governor for eight years, and minister for eight years – that is 24 years in top leadership positions! What can anybody point to that he was attracted to Evo Kingdom or Rivers State in all those 24 years? Nothing! Not one single thing!” Wike said. He drew a contrast with his own record. “I was a Minister of State for Education, and as I sit here, I can count the projects I brought to Rivers State and my people. But somebody was speaker, governor, and headed a very lucrative ministry as a full minister for eight years, yet brought nothing back home! How can someone who spent 24 years in power without empowering his people or raising new leaders now turn around to tell you he loves you?” he asked. Wike also reiterated his decision to resign as minister should President Bola Ahmed Tinubu lose in Rivers State and the FCT. He made the declaration at a strategic consultative meeting with stakeholders of Akpor Kingdom in Obio-Akpor on Friday, where he rallied the political structure of Rivers State behind the President. “My interest in Rivers State is for God to use me as a vessel to help our people. I am back here not for what I will get, but for what I will be to raise my people,” he said. He said politics was driven by the collective interest of the people and not by perpetual animosity. “There is no permanent enemy in politics; what we have is permanent collective interest. It is all about the interest of our people. The more you are in number, the happier you become. Leadership is like a wastebasket. If you cannot absorb things, both the good and the bad, then you cannot be a true leader,” he said. Wike told political actors in the state not to be distracted by social media criticism of his open-door policy towards former detractors, saying true political strength lies in numbers. He demanded an all-inclusive campaign structure across Obio-Akpor. “Whether you are a politician, whether you are a traditional ruler, whether you are a pastor, or whether you are a native doctor, I need everybody now,” he said, adding, “For the purpose of voting and elections, we must bring everyone together.” The post ‘Nothing to show after 24 years in power’, Wike knocks Amaechi. appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Navy dismantles illegal refinery, destroys site in Bonny
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Nigerian Navy has dismantled an illegal refining site and destroyed its equipment at Promise Land Community along Nanabie Creek in Bonny Local Government Area of Rivers State. The operation was carried out by the Forward Operating Base, FOB, Bonny, as part of efforts to disrupt illegal refining activities and deny criminal operators infrastructure used to process and store stolen crude oil. Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Commodore Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Friday, saying the illegal refining site was discovered on September 30 following credible intelligence. According to him, the site contained one large cooking pot and three large storage tanks believed to have been intended for illegal refining activities. “On 2 October 2026, the Commanding Officer, FOB Bonny, Captain SMC Umeh, led a team to the location, where the illegal refining site and associated equipment were destroyed in accordance with established regulations,” he said. Folorunsho said the operation represented another disruption of illegal refining capacity within the Bonny area, particularly through the removal of infrastructure that could be used to process and store stolen crude oil. He said the operation followed recent activities by FOB Bonny under Operation Delta Sentinel, which uncovered substantial volumes of suspected stolen crude oil and associated illegal refining infrastructure within its area of operations. “The Nigerian Navy has continued to strengthen surveillance and monitoring across the area to prevent the establishment or reactivation of illegal refining sites and deny criminal operators the infrastructure required to sustain crude oil theft and related activities,” he said. The post Navy dismantles illegal refinery, destroys site in Bonny appeared first on Vanguard News .
